weeks.title: KPIs and dashboards that drive decisions
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki business goal se sahi KPI kaise chunte hain, metric ko numerator, denominator aur time window ke saath precisely kaise define karte hain, KPI tree se revenue ko drivers me kaise todte hain, aur achha dashboard misleading dashboard se kaise alag hota hai.
concepts: **KPI vs metric**: har number KPI nahi hota. Metric koi bhi measurement hai (page views, calls, SKUs). **KPI (key performance indicator)** woh chhota set hai jo seedha business goal se juda ho, jiska ek owner ho, ek target ho, aur jiske hilne pe koi decision liya jaaye. Agar kisi number ke upar-neeche hone se koi action nahi badalta, toh woh dashboard ke top pe nahi hona chahiye.

**Leading vs lagging indicators**: lagging indicator result batata hai jab sab ho chuka (quarterly revenue, annual profit, last month ka churn). Leading indicator pehle hilta hai aur future result predict karta hai (free-trial sign-ups, sales pipeline value, cart additions, support ticket backlog). Achhe dashboard me dono hote hain: lagging se score pata chalta hai, leading se time pe action le sakte ho.

**Metric definition**: ek KPI ki poori definition me chaar cheezein hoti hain: numerator, denominator, time window aur grain (kis level pe: order, customer, store, din). Jaise 'conversion rate = orders / sessions, daily, sirf web channel'. 'Active user' ka matlab 30-day login hai ya 7-day purchase, yeh likhe bina do teams ke numbers kabhi match nahi karenge.

**Ratio of totals vs average of ratios**: overall conversion = Σ orders / Σ sessions hota hai, stores ke conversion % ka simple average nahi. Chhote store ka 15% aur bade store ka 2.5% barabar weight paayenge toh overall number jhootha bada ya chhota dikhega. Ratio KPI ko hamesha numerator aur denominator alag se sum karke roll-up karo.

**KPI tree (driver decomposition)**: Revenue = Sessions × Conversion rate × AOV (average order value = revenue / orders). Kyunki yeh product hai, growth factors multiply hote hain: (1 + g_revenue) = (1 + g_sessions)(1 + g_conversion)(1 + g_AOV). Isse pata chalta hai ki revenue kis driver ki wajah se badla aur kis team (marketing, product, pricing) ko action lena hai.

**Guardrail (counter) metrics aur Goodhart's law**: jab ek metric target ban jaata hai, log use game karne lagte hain ('when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure'). Isliye har primary KPI ke saath ek counter-metric rakho: tickets closed ke saath reopen rate, delivery speed ke saath damaged-order rate, sign-ups ke saath 30-day retention.

**Dashboard design**: pehle decision-question likho ('kya hum is hafte target pe hain?'), phir chart. Top pe 5–8 KPI tiles, har tile ke saath context: target, pichhla period, last year same period, aur ek chhoti trend line. RAG (red / amber / green) thresholds pehle se tay karo, drill-down (region → store) do, aur data kab refresh hua woh timestamp dikhao.

**Misleading dashboards**: bar chart ka y-axis 0 se na shuru karna (chhota farq bahut bada dikhta hai), do alag scales wala dual-axis chart (koi bhi correlation dikha sakte ho), cumulative chart (girti daily sales bhi upar jaati line lagti hai), 10 slices wala pie ya 3D chart, aur **vanity metrics** jaise 'total app downloads till date' jo hamesha badhte hain par engagement ke baare me kuch nahi batate.

example.problem: Kaveri Mart (fictional online grocery). September: 2,00,000 sessions, 6,400 orders, revenue ₹30,40,000. October: 2,40,000 sessions, 7,200 orders, revenue ₹36,00,000. Conversion aur AOV nikaalo, revenue growth ko drivers me todo, aur batao dashboard pe kya flag hona chahiye.
steps: Conversion = orders / sessions. September: 6,400 / 2,00,000 = 3.2%. October: 7,200 / 2,40,000 = 3.0%.
AOV = revenue / orders. September: 30,40,000 / 6,400 = ₹475. October: 36,00,000 / 7,200 = ₹500.
Check: 1.20 × 0.9375 × 1.0526 = 1.184, jo revenue growth se match karta hai. Percentages add karna (20 − 6.25 + 5.26 = 19.0%) galat hai kyunki tree multiplicative hai.

Interpretation: headline revenue green hai, par conversion gir raha hai; shayad naya traffic paid campaign se aaya jo kam convert karta hai. Conversion tile ko amber karo aur channel-wise drill-down dekho.
**Answer**: conversion **3.2% → 3.0%**, AOV **₹475 → ₹500**, revenue **+18.4%** = traffic aur AOV ki wajah se, jabki **conversion −6.25%** dashboard pe flag hona chahiye.

mistakes: Stores ya channels ke conversion % ka simple average leke overall conversion bolna. Fix: numerators aur denominators alag sum karo, phir divide karo (ratio of totals).
Bar chart ka axis 90 ya 95 se shuru karke chhote farq ko dramatic dikhana. Fix: bar chart hamesha 0 se; chhote changes dikhane hon toh line chart ya 'change in percentage points' wala tile use karo.
Sirf ek KPI ko target bana dena (jaise 'tickets closed per day'). Fix: har primary KPI ke saath ek guardrail metric rakho jo gaming pakad le (reopen rate, CSAT).
revision: KPI = goal se juda, owner + target + decision wala metric.
Lagging = result (revenue, churn); leading = pehle hilta hai (sign-ups, pipeline).
Ratio KPI roll-up: Σ numerator / Σ denominator, average of ratios nahi.
Revenue = sessions × conversion × AOV; growth factors multiply hote hain.
Har KPI ke saath context (target, last period) aur guardrail metric.
Bar axis 0 se, dual-axis aur cumulative charts se savdhaan.

questions.question: Ek subscription video app ka main goal agle quarter ka subscription revenue badhana hai. Inme se kaunsa **leading** indicator hai?
options: Pichhle quarter ka total subscription revenue
Is hafte shuru hue free trials ki sankhya
Pichhle mahine cancel hue subscribers ki sankhya
Pichhle financial year ka net profit
questions.explanation: Free trials aaj shuru hote hain aur kuch hafton baad paid subscriptions me badalte hain, isliye yeh future revenue pehle se batate hain: option B leading indicator hai. Trap: option C (pichhle mahine ke cancellations) bhi 'customer behaviour' lagta hai, par woh ho chuka result hai, yaani lagging; options A aur D bhi lagging financial results hain.

questions.question: Ek D2C brand ki website pe ek mahine me 1,60,000 sessions, 4,000 orders aur ₹18,00,000 revenue aaya. Conversion rate (orders / sessions) aur AOV kya hain?
options: Conversion 4%, AOV ₹450
Conversion 2.5%, AOV ₹11.25
Conversion 40%, AOV ₹4,500
Conversion 2.5%, AOV ₹450
questions.explanation: Conversion = 4,000 / 1,60,000 = 0.025 = 2.5%. AOV = revenue / orders = 18,00,000 / 4,000 = ₹450, isliye option D sahi hai. Trap: option B me AOV = revenue / sessions liya gaya (₹11.25 revenue per session hai, AOV nahi); options A aur C me decimal ya zero galat jagah lag gaya.

questions.question: Ek retail chain ke teen stores ka ek din ka data: Store P: 50 purchases / 1,000 visitors, Store Q: 30 / 200, Store R: 20 / 800. Chain ka overall visitor-to-purchase conversion kya hai?
questions.explanation: Overall = Σ purchases / Σ visitors = (50 + 30 + 20) / (1,000 + 200 + 800) = 100 / 2,000 = 5.0%, yaani option A. Trap: option B teen store rates (5%, 15%, 2.5%) ka simple average hai, jo chhote Store Q ko bade stores jitna weight de deta hai; options C aur D sirf ek store ka rate hain.

questions.question: Ek dashboard bar chart me Brand X ka customer satisfaction score 92 aur Brand Y ka 94 dikhata hai, par y-axis 90 se shuru hota hai. Chart me Y ka bar X se kitna lamba dikhta hai, aur asli farq kitna hai?
options: Dikhne me bhi aur asli me bhi lagbhag 2.2% lamba
Dikhne me 2.2% lamba, asli me 2 guna
Dikhne me 2 guna lamba, asli me sirf lagbhag 2.2% zyada
Dikhne me 4 guna lamba, asli me 2 points zyada
questions.explanation: Axis 90 se shuru hai, toh bar heights 92 − 90 = 2 aur 94 − 90 = 4 units hain: Y ka bar 2 guna dikhta hai. Asli ratio 94 / 92 = 1.022, yaani sirf lagbhag 2.2% zyada, isliye option C. Trap: option D me 4 ko ratio maan liya (4 sirf Y ke bar ki height hai); option A tab sahi hota jab axis 0 se shuru hota.

questions.question: Ek customer-support team ka naya KPI 'tickets closed per agent per day' hai aur iske saath bonus juda hai. Do mahine me yeh KPI 40% badh gaya, par complaints bhi badh gayi. Is problem ko pakadne ke liye sabse achha guardrail metric kaunsa hai?
options: 7 din ke andar reopen hone wale tickets ka percentage
Har agent ke total login hours
Har din aane wale naye tickets ki sankhya
Ek ticket close karne ka average time
questions.explanation: Bonus ki wajah se agents tickets bina solve kiye close kar sakte hain (Goodhart's law). Reopen rate (option A) seedha pakadta hai ki closed ticket sach me resolve hua ya nahi, isliye yeh sahi guardrail hai. Trap: option D (average handle time) bhi quality-related lagta hai, par jaldi-jaldi close karne se yeh aur 'achha' dikhega, gaming pakdega nahi; options B aur C effort aur demand naapte hain, quality nahi.

questions.question: Ek e-commerce site ka revenue = sessions × conversion rate × AOV. Agle mahine sessions 4% girne ka anumaan hai aur AOV same rahega. Revenue 10% badhane ke liye conversion rate ko lagbhag kitna (relative %) badhna hoga?
questions.explanation: Factors multiply hote hain: 0.96 × (1 + g) × 1 = 1.10, toh 1 + g = 1.10 / 0.96 = 1.1458, yaani g ≈ 14.6%, option C. Trap: option A percentages ko add/subtract karke aata hai (10 + 4 = 14%), jo multiplicative tree me galat hai; option B (10 − 4) sign bhi ulta le leta hai, aur option D sessions ki giravat ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Ek fitness app ki leadership dashboard ke top pe ek number rakhna chahti hai. Inme se kaunsa **vanity metric** hai jo engagement ke baare me sabse kam batata hai?
options: Naye users ka 30-day retention rate
Total users me weekly active users ka share
Launch se ab tak total app downloads
Members ka repeat workout booking rate
questions.explanation: Total downloads till date (option C) hamesha badhta hi rehta hai, chahe log app khol hi na rahe hon, isliye yeh vanity metric hai. Trap: option B bhi 'users' ka number lagta hai, par yeh active users ka share hai jo gir bhi sakta hai aur engagement dikhata hai; options A aur D retention aur repeat behaviour naapte hain, jo asli decision-wale KPIs hain.

questions.question: Ek B2B software company ke dashboard ke chaar numbers me se kaunsa **lagging** indicator hai?
options: Is hafte aaye demo requests
Pichhle quarter me churn hua annual revenue
Sales pipeline me open deals ki value
Is mahine shuru hue free trials
questions.explanation: Pichhle quarter ka churned revenue (option B) ek ho chuka result hai, isliye lagging hai. Trap: option C (pipeline value) bhi rupees me hai aur financial lagta hai, par yeh future deals ka signal hai, yaani leading; options A aur D bhi aage aane wale revenue ko pehle se batate hain.

questions.question: Ek hi company ki do teams monthly review me 'active users' report karti hain: Product team 52,000 aur Finance team 38,000. Dono ka data source same hai. Is mismatch ki sabse sambhav wajah kya hai?
options: 'Active' ki definition alag hai (login vs purchase)
Ek team ka database server bahut slow hai
Finance team ne bade numbers round off kar diye
Dono dashboards ka chart type alag hai
questions.explanation: Same source se itna bada farq (52,000 vs 38,000) tab aata hai jab metric definition alag ho: kaunsa event 'active' ginta hai aur time window kitni hai. Isliye option A sahi hai; KPI ki poori definition (numerator, denominator, time window, grain) likhni chahiye. Trap: option C rounding sirf chhota farq laata hai, hazaron ka nahi; options B aur D presentation ya speed ki baatein hain, number badalti nahi.

questions.question: Ek bakery chain ki daily sales (units) paanch din me 500, 480, 450, 420, 400 rahi. Dashboard pe inka **cumulative** line chart lagaya gaya. Chart kya dikhayega, aur asli trend kya hai?
options: Line 500 se 400 tak girti hai; asli trend bhi 20% giravat hai
Line 2,250 pe flat rehti hai; sales stable hain
Line 500 se 2,250 tak chadhti hai; asli sales 125% badhi
Line 500 se 2,250 tak chadhti hai, jabki daily sales 20% giri
questions.explanation: Cumulative values: 500, 980, 1,430, 1,850, 2,250, toh line lagataar upar jaati hai. Asli daily sales 500 se 400 hui, yaani 400 / 500 − 1 = −20%, isliye option D. Trap: option C upar jaati line ko growth samajh leta hai (2,250 total hai, growth nahi); option A daily chart ka description hai, cumulative ka nahi.

questions.question: Ek online store ke agle mahine ke plan me sessions +10%, conversion rate +5% (relative) aur AOV −8% hai. Revenue = sessions × conversion × AOV. Revenue ka expected change kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Tree multiplicative hai: 1.10 × 1.05 × 0.92 = 1.0626, yaani revenue lagbhag +6.3% (option B). Trap: option A percentages add karta hai (10 + 5 − 8 = 7%), jo product tree me galat hai; option C conversion ko bhool jaata hai (1.10 × 0.92 = 1.012), aur option D AOV ki giravat ko bhi plus maan leta hai.

questions.question: Tulsi Bazaar (fictional) ka data. Month 1: 5,00,000 sessions, conversion 2.4%, AOV ₹600. Month 2: 4,50,000 sessions, 12,150 orders, revenue ₹70,47,000. Revenue ka % change kya hai, aur kaunsa driver sabse zyada (relative) badla?
options: Revenue −2.1%; conversion +12.5% sabse bada move
Revenue −2.1%; sessions −10% sabse bada move
Revenue −0.8%; conversion +12.5% sabse bada move
Revenue +2.1%; AOV −3.3% sabse bada move
questions.explanation: Month 1: orders = 5,00,000 × 0.024 = 12,000, revenue = 12,000 × 600 = ₹72,00,000. Month 2: conversion = 12,150 / 4,50,000 = 2.7%, AOV = 70,47,000 / 12,150 = ₹580. Factors: sessions 0.90 (−10%), conversion 2.7 / 2.4 = 1.125 (+12.5%), AOV 580 / 600 = 0.967 (−3.3%). Revenue = 70,47,000 / 72,00,000 − 1 = −2.1%, aur sabse bada move conversion ka hai: option A. Trap: option C drivers ko add karta hai (−10 + 12.5 − 3.3 ≈ −0.8%); option B sirf absolute sign dekh ke sessions ko bada bolta hai, jabki 12.5 > 10.

questions.question: Ek support team ka KPI 'SLA ke andar resolved tickets %' hai, RAG rule: ≥ 85% Green, 80–85% Amber, < 80% Red. Is hafte: Agent P 170 / 200, Q 9 / 10, R 19 / 20, S 240 / 320. Team ka sahi SLA % aur RAG status kya hai?
options: 86.25%, Green
80.0%, Amber
87.5%, Green
questions.explanation: Ratio of totals: (170 + 9 + 19 + 240) / (200 + 10 + 20 + 320) = 438 / 550 = 79.6%, jo 80% se neeche hai, toh Red (option B). Trap: option A chaar agent rates (85, 90, 95, 75) ka simple average hai, jo chhote Q aur R ko bade S jitna weight deta hai aur galti se Green dikhata hai; option D un rates ka median hai, aur option C sirf P aur S ka average hai.

questions.question: Ek store pe abhi 2,00,000 sessions/mahina aate hain, conversion 3%. Ek paid campaign 50,000 extra sessions laayega jo sirf 1.5% convert karte hain. AOV same rehta hai. Campaign ke baad overall conversion aur revenue growth kya hogi?
options: Conversion 3% hi rahegi, revenue +25%
Conversion 2.25%, revenue +12.5%
Conversion 2.7%, revenue +12.5%
Conversion 2.7%, revenue +25%
questions.explanation: Orders: 2,00,000 × 0.03 = 6,000 purane + 50,000 × 0.015 = 750 naye = 6,750. Overall conversion = 6,750 / 2,50,000 = 2.7%. AOV same hai toh revenue growth = orders growth = 6,750 / 6,000 − 1 = 12.5%, isliye option C. Trap: option B 3% aur 1.5% ka simple average leta hai (ratio of totals nahi); options A aur D sessions ki +25% growth ko seedha revenue maan lete hain aur conversion ki giravat ignore karte hain.

questions.question: Ek ₹499/mahina wale app me free trial 14 din ka hai. Pichhle mahine 1,500 trials shuru hue aur 25% paid bane. Is mahine 1,200 trials shuru hue, aur early data ke hisaab se 30% paid banenge. Is mahine ke trials se kitna naya MRR aayega, aur pichhle cohort se tulna?
options: ₹1,49,700; pichhle cohort se 20% kam
₹2,24,550; pichhle cohort se 20% zyada
₹1,79,640; pichhle cohort ke barabar
₹1,79,640; pichhle cohort se 4% kam
questions.explanation: Is mahine: 1,200 × 0.30 × 499 = ₹1,79,640. Pichhla cohort: 1,500 × 0.25 × 499 = ₹1,87,125. Ratio = 1,79,640 / 1,87,125 = 0.96, yaani 4% kam: option D. Trap: option C sochta hai ki trials −20% aur conversion +20% (25 → 30) cancel ho jaate hain, par factors multiply hote hain (0.8 × 1.2 = 0.96); option A purana 25% rate lagata hai aur option B purane 1,500 trials.

weeks.title: Segmentation, pivots and Simpson's paradox
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki data ko segments aur pivot tables me kaise todte hain, sahi denominator kaise chunte hain, overall number me mix effect aur rate effect ko kaise alag karte hain, aur Simpson's paradox jaise cases me summary kaise dhokha deti hai.
concepts: **Segmentation**: customers ya transactions ko aise groups me baantna jinka behaviour alag ho: geographic (metro / tier-2), demographic (age band), behavioural (**RFM**: recency, frequency, monetary value) ya channel (app / web). Achha segment measurable, kaafi bada, baaki segments se alag, aur actionable hota hai, yaani us par alag offer ya process chal sake.

**Pivot table / group-by**: rows (jaise city), columns (jaise channel), values (jaise order value) aur aggregation (sum, mean, count, distinct count) chunke ek hi raw table se alag-alag summary banti hai. Aggregation sawaal se tay hoti hai: 'kitna revenue?' → sum; 'typical order kitna bada?' → mean ya median; 'kitne customers?' → distinct count, kyunki ek customer ke kai orders ho sakte hain.

**Row % vs column % vs total %**: ek hi cell ka percentage teen denominators se ban sakta hai. 'North ke kitne % customers Premium hain' ka denominator North ka row total hai; 'Premium customers me se kitne % North se hain' ka denominator Premium ka column total hai. Report me denominator hamesha naam se likho.

**Percent vs percentage points**: return rate 8% se 10% hua toh change **2 percentage points (pp)** hai, aur relative change 2 / 8 = 25% hai. Dono sahi hain par alag cheezein hain; 'returns 2% badhe' likhna ambiguous hai.

**Mix effect vs rate effect**: overall average = Σ (segment ka share × segment ka rate). Overall number do wajah se badal sakta hai: segment ke andar rate badla (rate effect), ya segments ke shares badle (mix effect). Isliye har segment ka AOV badhe tab bhi overall AOV gir sakta hai, agar sasta segment tezi se bada ho gaya.

**Simpson's paradox**: har segment me A, B se behtar ho, phir bhi combine karne pe B behtar dikhe. Yeh tab hota hai jab ek lurking variable (segment) dono se juda ho: kis group me kitne units gaye, aur outcome kitna aasaan tha. Hal: pehle causal story socho; agar segment ek confounder hai toh segment-wise compare karo ya standardise karo.

**Direct standardisation**: dono groups ke segment-rates ko ek hi common mix (jaise combined population ka mix) pe apply karo. Isse 'kis group ko aasaan cases mile' ka farq hat jaata hai aur rates fair tareeke se compare hote hain.

**Summaries kab mislead karti hain**: chhote denominators (4 me se 3 = 75% wala store top rank pe), skewed data me mean (kuch bade orders mean ko kheench lete hain; median bhi dikhao), survivorship bias (sirf abhi active customers ka average), aur ecological fallacy (state-level correlation ko individual customers pe laga dena).

example.problem: Do delivery partners (fictional): SwiftKart: metro 720 / 800 on-time, tier-2 140 / 200 on-time. DakDost: metro 184 / 200 on-time, tier-2 600 / 800 on-time. Overall kaun behtar dikhta hai, segment-wise kaun behtar hai, aur common 50-50 mix pe standardised rates kya hain?
steps: Segment-wise DakDost dono jagah aage hai (92 > 90, 75 > 70), par overall SwiftKart aage dikhta hai (86 > 78.4): yeh Simpson's paradox hai.
Wajah: DakDost ke 80% orders tier-2 me hain jahan on-time delivery mushkil hai, jabki SwiftKart ke sirf 20% orders tier-2 me hain. Segment (city type) ek confounder hai.
Combined mix: metro 1000 / 2000 = 50%, tier-2 50%. SwiftKart standardised = 0.5 × 90 + 0.5 × 70 = 80%.
DakDost standardised = 0.5 × 92 + 0.5 × 75 = 83.5%.

**Answer**: crude overall me SwiftKart (**86% vs 78.4%**) aage dikhta hai, par same mix pe DakDost **83.5% vs 80%** se behtar hai; partner choose karne ke liye segment-wise ya standardised comparison use karo.

mistakes: Do groups ke overall rates compare karke decision lena bina dekhe ki unka segment mix alag hai. Fix: pehle segment-wise table banao; mix bahut alag ho toh standardised rates compare karo.
Percentage points aur percent ko mix karna ('conversion 4% se 5% hua, yaani 1% badha'). Fix: absolute change pp me likho aur relative change % me, dono saaf-saaf.
Chhote denominator wale segment ko top performer bata dena. Fix: rate ke saath hamesha n bhi dikhao aur ranking ke liye minimum sample size rakho.
revision: Pivot = rows × columns × values × aggregation; aggregation sawaal se tay hoti hai.
Row % aur column % ke denominators alag hote hain; naam se likho.
8% → 10% = +2 pp = +25% relative.
Overall = Σ share × rate; overall change = rate effect + mix effect.
Simpson's paradox: segment-wise trend combine karne pe ulta; confounder dhoondo.
Standardisation: dono groups ke rates ko ek common mix pe lagao.

questions.question: Ek fashion e-tailer ka return rate is quarter 8% se badhkar 10% ho gaya. Is change ko sahi tarah se kaise describe karenge?
options: 2 percentage points, jo 2% relative increase bhi hai
25 percentage points ka increase
2 percentage points ka increase, yaani 25% relative increase
10 percentage points ka increase, yaani 125% relative increase
questions.explanation: Absolute change = 10 − 8 = 2 percentage points; relative change = 2 / 8 = 0.25 = 25%, isliye option C. Trap: option A pp aur relative % ko same maan leta hai (2 pp ka relative matlab 25% hai, 2% nahi); option B relative 25% ko galti se pp me likh deta hai.

questions.question: Ek loyalty programme me 300 Gold members ka average monthly spend ₹800 hai aur 700 Silver members ka ₹400. Saare 1,000 members ka average monthly spend kya hai?
questions.explanation: Weighted average = (300 × 800 + 700 × 400) / 1,000 = (2,40,000 + 2,80,000) / 1,000 = ₹520, yaani option A. Trap: option B do segment averages ka simple average hai, jo bade Silver segment ko kam weight deta hai; option C weights ulte laga deta hai (0.7 × 800 + 0.3 × 400); option D do averages ka sum hai.

questions.question: Do sales reps ke lead conversions (fictional data): Asha: warm leads 45 / 60, cold leads 12 / 140. Bilal: warm leads 120 / 180, cold leads 1 / 20. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Bilal dono lead types me Asha se behtar hai, isliye overall bhi aage hai
Asha overall aur dono lead types me, teeno jagah aage hai
Dono ka overall conversion barabar hai, kyunki dono ke 200 leads hain
Asha har lead type me behtar hai, par Bilal overall aage hai kyunki uske 90% leads warm hain
questions.explanation: Asha: warm 75%, cold 8.6%, overall 57 / 200 = 28.5%. Bilal: warm 66.7%, cold 5%, overall 121 / 200 = 60.5%. Asha har segment me aage, par Bilal ko 180 / 200 = 90% warm (aasaan) leads mile, isliye overall Bilal aage: option D (Simpson's paradox). Trap: option A sirf overall number dekh ke maan leta hai ki Bilal har jagah behtar hai; option C equal lead count ko equal conversion samajh leta hai.

questions.question: Ek food brand (fictional) ke orders: pichhle saal App 600 orders AOV ₹500, Web 400 orders AOV ₹900. Is saal App 1,500 orders AOV ₹520, Web 500 orders AOV ₹950. Is saal ka overall AOV kya hai, aur pichhle saal ke ₹660 se tulna me kya hua?
options: ₹692; dono channels ka AOV badha, isliye overall bhi badha
₹627.50; dono channels ka AOV badha, phir bhi mix sasta App ki taraf shift hone se overall gira
₹735; overall AOV badha
₹660; overall AOV same raha
questions.explanation: Is saal overall = (1,500 × 520 + 500 × 950) / 2,000 = (7,80,000 + 4,75,000) / 2,000 = ₹627.50, jo ₹660 se kam hai. App ka share 60% se 75% ho gaya: mix effect ne rate effect ko dabaa diya, isliye option B. Trap: option A pichhle saal ka 60:40 mix use karta hai (0.6 × 520 + 0.4 × 950 = 692); option C do AOVs ka simple average hai.

questions.question: Ek SaaS company ke 1,000 customers: North me 120 Premium + 280 Basic, South me 80 Premium + 520 Basic. Board poochta hai: 'Premium customers me se kitne % North se hain?'
questions.explanation: Sawaal ka denominator Premium column total hai: 120 + 80 = 200. North Premium = 120, toh 120 / 200 = 60%, option A. Trap: option B row % hai (North ke 400 customers me se 120 = 30% Premium), jo ulta sawaal answer karta hai; option C total % hai (120 / 1,000); option D South ka share hai.

questions.question: Do discount strategies (fictional) alag stores me test hui. Strategy P: urban stores me 30% redemption (900 customers), rural me 10% (100 customers). Strategy Q: urban 32% (200 customers), rural 12% (800 customers). Combined customer mix (urban 1,100, rural 900) pe standardise karke kaunsi strategy kitne percentage points se behtar hai?
options: P, 12 percentage points se
Q, 2 percentage points se
Dono barabar hain
Q, 4 percentage points se

weeks.title: Brand preference across cities: the chi-square test of independence
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki do categorical variables (jaise city aur brand) ke beech association ko contingency table aur chi-square test of independence se kaise test karte hain, kaun se cells result ko drive kar rahe hain yeh residuals se kaise dekhte hain, aur Cramér's V se association ki strength kaise naapte hain.
concepts: **Contingency table (cross-tab)**: do categorical variables ke combinations ke counts, jaise rows = city, columns = preferred brand. Business sawaal: 'kya brand preference city pe depend karti hai?' **H₀**: city aur brand independent hain (har city me brand shares same hain). **H₁**: dono associated hain (kam se kam ek city ka brand mix alag hai).

**Expected count**: agar H₀ sach hai toh P(row aur column) = P(row) × P(column), isliye E = (row total × column total) / N. Expected counts woh table hai jo 'koi association nahi' wali duniya me dikhti; test observed (O) ko is E se compare karta hai.

**Chi-square statistic**: χ² = Σ (O − E)² / E, saare cells pe. Har cell ka **contribution** (O − E)² / E hota hai. **df = (r − 1)(c − 1)**. Test hamesha right-tailed hai: χ² critical value se bada (ya p-value < α) ho toh H₀ reject. Jaise df = 4 pe 5% critical value 9.488 hai.

**Conditions**: observations independent hon aur har customer sirf ek cell me gine, table me **counts** hon (percentages ya averages nahi), aur expected counts kaafi bade hon: rule of thumb, saare E ≥ 5 (ya kam se kam 80% cells me E ≥ 5 aur koi E < 1 nahi). Warna chhoti categories merge karo, ya 2×2 me Fisher's exact test use karo.

**Standardised (Pearson) residual** = (O − E) / √E. Iska sign batata hai cell expected se zyada (+) hai ya kam (−), aur |residual| > 2 wale cells association ko drive karte hain. Sirf 'significant' bolna kaafi nahi; manager ko batana hai ki kaunsi city kis brand ko over-index karti hai.

**Cramér's V (effect size)** = √(χ² / (N × (k − 1))), jahan k = min(rows, columns); 2×2 me yeh φ ban jaata hai. χ² sample size ke saath badhta hai: same proportions aur 4 guna data ⇒ 4 guna χ². V size-free hai: lagbhag 0.1 weak, 0.3 moderate, 0.5 strong association (rough guide).

**Independence vs homogeneity vs goodness-of-fit**: ek random sample ko do variables pe classify kiya → independence test. Har city se alag fixed sample liya → homogeneity test (arithmetic same). Ek hi variable ko kisi claimed distribution se compare karna (jaise 'teen brands ka share 50 : 30 : 20') → goodness-of-fit, df = categories − 1.

**Business reading**: association ka matlab causation nahi. Pune ka ek brand ko zyada pasand karna income, distribution reach ya local taste ki wajah se ho sakta hai. Result se action nikaalo (regional campaign, shelf allocation), par cause ko alag test ya experiment se confirm karo.

example.problem: Ek tea company (fictional) ne 400 customers se poocha ki woh kaunsa brand pasand karte hain. Chennai (150): Neelgiri Gold 70, Brahmaputra Leaf 50, Sahyadri Chai 30. Kolkata (120): 40, 60, 20. Pune (130): 40, 40, 50. 5% level pe test karo ki brand preference city se independent hai ya nahi (df = 4 pe critical value 9.488), aur batao kaun se cells result ko drive karte hain.
steps: Column totals: Neelgiri 150, Brahmaputra 150, Sahyadri 100; N = 400.
Expected counts (row × column / N): Chennai 56.25, 56.25, 37.5; Kolkata 45, 45, 30; Pune 48.75, 48.75, 32.5.
Contributions: Chennai 3.36, 0.69, 1.50; Kolkata 0.56, 5.00, 3.33; Pune 1.57, 1.57, 9.42.
χ² = sum ≈ 27.01, df = (3 − 1)(3 − 1) = 4. 27.01 > 9.488, toh H₀ reject: brand preference city ke saath associated hai.
Standardised residuals: Pune–Sahyadri = (50 − 32.5) / √32.5 ≈ +3.07 aur Kolkata–Brahmaputra = (60 − 45) / √45 ≈ +2.24 sabse bade hain.
Cramér's V = √(27.01 / (400 × 2)) ≈ 0.18, yaani association real hai par weak-to-moderate.
**Answer**: **χ² ≈ 27.0 > 9.488**, H₀ reject; association mainly **Pune ka Sahyadri Chai** aur **Kolkata ka Brahmaputra Leaf** ki taraf jhukaav se aata hai, aur **V ≈ 0.18**.

mistakes: Counts ki jagah percentages ya averages pe χ² lagana. Fix: hamesha raw frequencies use karo; percentages se χ² ki value N ke hisaab se galat aati hai.
Sirf 'p < 0.05, significant' bolke ruk jaana. Fix: residuals se batao kaunse cells drive kar rahe hain, aur Cramér's V se strength; bade N me tiny association bhi significant hoti hai.
Expected counts 5 se kam hone pe bhi test chala dena. Fix: rare categories merge karo (jaise 'Others'), ya chhoti 2×2 tables me Fisher's exact test lo.
revision: H₀: dono categorical variables independent.
E = row total × column total / N.
χ² = Σ (O − E)² / E, df = (r − 1)(c − 1), right-tailed.
Standardised residual (O − E) / √E; |r| > 2 drive karta hai.
Cramér's V = √(χ² / (N(k − 1))), k = min(r, c).
Same proportions, 4 guna N ⇒ 4 guna χ², V same.

questions.question: Ek beverage company 4 cities aur 3 brands ki contingency table pe chi-square test of independence chalaati hai. Degrees of freedom kitne honge?

Option B (150 / 4) aur option D (150 × 150 / 400) galat totals use karte hain.

Trap: option C df = 2 ka critical value lagata hai (2×2 table me df = 1); option A sirf ek row ke cells jodta hai; option D association ko causation bana deta hai.

questions.explanation: k = min(3, 4) = 3, toh V = √(χ² / (N(k − 1))) = √(24 / (300 × 2)) = √0.04 = 0.20, option C. Trap: option A √ lena bhool jaata hai; option B (k − 1) bhool ke √(24 / 300) leta hai; option D k − 1 ki jagah k = 3 use karta hai.

questions.question: Survey 1: Delhi (100) me 55 X / 45 Y, Mumbai (100) me 45 X / 55 Y. Survey 2 me har cell 4 guna hai: Delhi 220 / 180, Mumbai 180 / 220. df = 1 pe 5% critical value 3.841 hai. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Survey 1 me χ² = 2.0 (not significant), Survey 2 me χ² = 8.0 (significant), par φ (Cramér's V) dono me 0.1 hi hai
Dono surveys me χ² = 2.0, kyunki proportions same hain
Survey 2 me χ² = 8.0 aur φ bhi 4 guna hoke 0.4 ho gaya, yaani strong association

Survey 2: E = 200, χ² = 4 × 20² / 200 = 8.0 > 3.841. φ = √(χ² / N) = √(2 / 200) = √(8 / 800) = 0.1 dono me, isliye option A. Trap: option C maan leta hai ki effect size bhi N ke saath badhta hai; χ² badha kyunki evidence badha, association ki strength wahi hai. Option B bhool jaata hai ki χ² counts pe depend karta hai.

questions.question: Ek analyst city aur preferred snack brand ke beech association test karna chahta hai. Chi-square test of independence ke liye table ke cells me kya hona chahiye?

questions.question: Ek paint company ne Lucknow, Nagpur aur Kochi teeno se **alag-alag fixed 200 customers** chune aur poocha ki woh kaunsa finish (matte / gloss / satin) pasand karte hain. Yeh kaunsa chi-square test hai?

weeks.title: Comparing groups: two-sample tests, A/B tests and one-way ANOVA
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki do groups ke means ko Welch t-test se, do conversion rates ko two-proportion z-test se, aur teen ya zyada groups ko one-way ANOVA se kaise compare karte hain, multiple testing ka risk kaise control karte hain, aur effect size se business importance kaise judge karte hain.
concepts: **Design pehle, test baad me**: outcome numeric hai (delivery time, basket size) ya binary (converted / not)? Groups independent hain (alag customers, alag stores) ya same units do baar measure hue (paired, jo week 9 me aayega)? Do groups ke means → two-sample t; do proportions → two-proportion z; teen ya zyada groups ke means → one-way ANOVA.

**Welch two-sample t-test**: t = (x̄₁ − x̄₂) / √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂). Yeh equal variances assume nahi karta, aur df Welch–Satterthwaite formula se aata hai: df = (v₁ + v₂)² / (v₁²/(n₁ − 1) + v₂²/(n₂ − 1)), jahan vᵢ = sᵢ²/nᵢ. **Pooled t** tabhi lo jab SDs aur sample sizes milte-julte hon; business data me Welch safe default hai.

**A/B test for conversion (two-proportion z-test)**: H₀: p_A = p_B. Pooled p̂ = (x_A + x_B) / (n_A + n_B), SE = √(p̂(1 − p̂)(1/n_A + 1/n_B)), z = (p̂_B − p̂_A) / SE. '25% relative lift' sunne me bada lagta hai, par chhote base rate aur chhote n pe yeh noise bhi ho sakta hai. Test one-sided hai ya two-sided, yeh data dekhne se pehle tay karo.

**One-way ANOVA**: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = … = μ_k; H₁: kam se kam ek mean alag. Total variation todo: SST = SSB (between groups) + SSW (within groups). MSB = SSB / (k − 1), MSW = SSW / (N − k), **F = MSB / MSW**. Agar groups me asli farq nahi toh F ≈ 1; F critical value se bada ho toh H₀ reject.

**Multiple t-tests kyun nahi**: har test α = 0.05 pe ho aur m independent tests hon toh kam se kam ek false positive ka chance (family-wise error rate) = 1 − (1 − α)^m. 3 groups ke 3 pairwise tests me yeh lagbhag 14.3% ho jaata hai. ANOVA ek hi F-test se overall sawaal 5% pe answer karta hai.

**Post-hoc comparisons**: significant F sirf batata hai ki koi farq hai, kaunsa pair alag hai yeh nahi. Phir Tukey HSD ya **Bonferroni** (har pair ko α / m pe test karo, m = k(k − 1)/2) use karo. 4 groups ⇒ 6 pairs ⇒ har test 0.05 / 6 ≈ 0.0083 pe.

**Assumptions**: groups ke andar observations independent, har group lagbhag normal (n bada ho toh CLT madad karta hai), aur variances roughly equal (Levene's test; rule of thumb: sabse badi SD / sabse chhoti SD < 2). Variances bahut alag hon toh Welch ANOVA, aur heavy outliers ya ordinal data ho toh Kruskal–Wallis.

**Effect size**: η² = SSB / SST = outcome ke variation ka kitna hissa group membership explain karti hai; do groups ke liye Cohen's d = (x̄₁ − x̄₂) / pooled SD. Bade sample me tiny farq bhi significant ho jaata hai; rollout ka decision effect size aur cost se lo, sirf p-value se nahi.

example.problem: QuickBasket (fictional) do dark-store models test karta hai. Model A: 25 stores, average delivery time 38 min, s = 6. Model B: 20 stores, average 32 min, s = 10. 5% two-sided level pe Welch t-test se batao kya farq significant hai (df = 29 pe t critical 2.045).
steps: Welch df = 6.44² / (1.44² / 24 + 5² / 19) ≈ 29.6; conservative rehne ke liye 29 lo.
|t| = 2.36 > 2.045, toh H₀ (equal means) reject.
Note: SDs 6 vs 10 kaafi alag hain, isliye pooled t (jo t ≈ 2.49 deta) ki jagah Welch sahi choice hai.
**Answer**: **t ≈ 2.36 > 2.045**, Model B ka delivery time significantly kam hai; average farq **6 minute** hai, jo ab cost ke saath tolna hai.

mistakes: Teen ya zyada groups me saare pairs pe alag-alag t-test chala dena. Fix: pehle ANOVA F-test, phir Tukey ya Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc comparisons.
Significant F ka matlab 'saare groups ek doosre se alag hain' samajhna. Fix: F sirf itna kehta hai ki kam se kam ek mean alag hai; kaunse pairs alag hain yeh post-hoc batata hai.
A/B test me bada relative lift dekh ke winner declare karna. Fix: z-test (ya confidence interval) se check karo, aur sample size test shuru hone se pehle tay karo.
revision: Welch t: SE = √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂); unequal variances me safe.
Two-proportion z: pooled p̂ se SE, z = (p̂_B − p̂_A) / SE.
ANOVA: F = [SSB / (k − 1)] / [SSW / (N − k)].
FWER = 1 − (1 − α)^m; Bonferroni: α / m.
Significant F ⇒ kam se kam ek mean alag; post-hoc se pair dhoondo.
η² = SSB / SST, effect size ke saath decision lo.

questions.question: Ek analyst 3 store formats ke average bill ko compare karne ke liye 3 pairwise t-tests chalaata hai, har ek α = 0.05 pe. Agar tests independent maane jaayein aur asal me koi farq na ho, toh kam se kam ek false positive aane ki probability kya hai?
options: Lagbhag 14.3%
questions.explanation: FWER = 1 − (1 − 0.05)³ = 1 − 0.857375 ≈ 0.143, yaani lagbhag 14.3%, option D. Trap: option B 3 × 0.05 jod deta hai; yeh sirf upper bound (Bonferroni inequality) hai, exact probability nahi. Option A maan leta hai ki har test ka 5% poore analysis pe bhi 5% hi rehta hai.

questions.question: Ek company 4 ad campaigns ka sales lift compare karti hai; har campaign 5 alag stores me chala (total 20 stores). One-way ANOVA ke F-statistic ke degrees of freedom kya hain?
questions.explanation: Between-groups df = k − 1 = 4 − 1 = 3; within-groups df = N − k = 20 − 4 = 16, isliye F(3, 16), option B. Trap: option C total df (N − 1 = 19) ko within df maan leta hai; options A aur D groups ki sankhya ko hi df le lete hain.

questions.question: 4 pricing plans, har plan me 10 customers (N = 40). ANOVA me SSB = 120 aur SSW = 360 aaye. F(3, 36) ka 5% critical value 2.866 hai. Sahi conclusion kya hai?
options: F ≈ 0.33, H₀ reject nahi hota
F = 12.0, H₀ reject
F = 4.0, H₀ reject: kam se kam ek plan ka mean baaki se alag hai
F = 4.0, H₀ reject: chaaron plans ke means ek doosre se alag hain
questions.explanation: MSB = 120 / 3 = 40, MSW = 360 / 36 = 10, F = 40 / 10 = 4.0 > 2.866, toh reject; ANOVA sirf itna kehta hai ki kam se kam ek mean alag hai, isliye option C. Trap: option D wahi F leta hai par conclusion zyada kheench deta hai; kaunse pairs alag hain yeh post-hoc test batayega. Option B SSB ko df se divide karna bhool jaata hai (120 / 10), aur option A SSB / SSW leta hai.

questions.question: Ek checkout page A/B test: version A me 2,000 visitors se 120 orders, version B me 2,000 visitors se 150 orders. Pooled two-proportion z-test (two-sided, α = 0.05, critical value 1.96) ka sahi result kya hai?
options: z ≈ 1.89; 5% two-sided level pe significant nahi
z ≈ 1.89; significant, kyunki relative lift 25% hai
z ≈ 2.67; significant
z ≈ 1.89; significant, kyunki 1.89 > 1.645
questions.explanation: p̂_A = 0.06, p̂_B = 0.075, pooled p̂ = 270 / 4,000 = 0.0675. SE = √(0.0675 × 0.9325 × (1/2,000 + 1/2,000)) ≈ 0.00793. z = 0.015 / 0.00793 ≈ 1.89 < 1.96, isliye option A. Trap: option D one-sided critical value (1.645) laga deta hai jabki test two-sided tay tha; option C SE me sirf ek 1/n leta hai; option B lift ke size ko significance samajh leta hai.

questions.question: 4 delivery partners ke ANOVA me F significant aaya. Ab saare pairwise comparisons Bonferroni correction ke saath karne hain, family-wise α = 0.05. Har pairwise test kis significance level pe hoga?
options: Lagbhag 0.0083
Lagbhag 0.0167
questions.explanation: 4 groups me pairs m = 4 × 3 / 2 = 6, toh har test α / m = 0.05 / 6 ≈ 0.0083 pe, option B. Trap: option A groups ki sankhya (4) se divide karta hai, pairs ki sankhya se nahi; option D 3 comparisons maan leta hai; option C correction hi nahi lagata.

questions.question: Ek supermarket chain (fictional) ne 3 shelf layouts 12 stores me test kiye (har layout 4 stores). Weekly sales (₹ lakh) neeche diye hain. One-way ANOVA ka F aur η² kya hai, aur 5% pe (F(2, 9) critical = 4.256) decision kya hai?
options: F ≈ 1.72, H₀ reject nahi; η² ≈ 0.63
F ≈ 7.75, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 1.72
F ≈ 15.5, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 0.63
F ≈ 7.75, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 0.63
questions.explanation: Means 11.5, 14.5, 12; grand mean 12.667. SSB = 4 × (1.167² + 1.833² + 0.667²) ≈ 20.67. SSW = 5 + 5 + 2 = 12. MSB = 20.67 / 2 = 10.33, MSW = 12 / 9 = 1.333, F ≈ 7.75 > 4.256 ⇒ reject. η² = 20.67 / 32.67 ≈ 0.63, isliye option D. Trap: option C SSB ko df = 2 se divide karna bhool jaata hai; option A SSB / SSW ko F maan leta hai; option B wahi ratio η² ke roop me leta hai, jabki η² ka denominator SST hai.

questions.question: Ek insurance website do landing pages test karti hai. Har visitor ke liye outcome sirf 'quote liya / nahi liya' hai, aur dono pages pe alag visitors hain. Kaunsa test sahi hai?
options: Two-proportion z-test
Welch two-sample t-test
One-way ANOVA
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test
questions.explanation: Outcome binary hai aur do independent groups hain, isliye do proportions compare karne wala two-proportion z-test (option A) sahi hai. Trap: option B numeric outcome (jaise average premium) ke means ke liye hai; option C teen ya zyada groups ke means ke liye, aur option D ek hi variable ko claimed distribution se compare karta hai.

questions.question: Teen store formats ke average basket value pe ANOVA chalana hai. Group SDs: ₹4, ₹5 aur ₹11 (hundreds me). Rule of thumb ke hisaab se kya karna chahiye?
options: Normal one-way ANOVA, kyunki 3 groups hain
Teen pairwise pooled t-tests
Normal ANOVA, kyunki teeno SDs 15 se kam hain
Welch ANOVA, kyunki SD ratio 11 / 4 = 2.75 > 2 hai
questions.explanation: Equal-variance check: sabse badi SD / sabse chhoti SD = 11 / 4 = 2.75, jo 2 se zyada hai, isliye variances barabar nahi maan sakte aur Welch ANOVA (option D) lena chahiye. Trap: option A aur C equal-variance assumption ko ignore karte hain (rule ratio pe hai, kisi absolute SD pe nahi); option B multiple t-tests ka error rate badhata hai aur pooled variance bhi wahi galat assumption hai.

questions.question: Ek naye onboarding flow se average session time 6 minute badha. Dono groups ki pooled SD 12 minute hai. Cohen's d kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cohen's d = (x̄₁ − x̄₂) / pooled SD = 6 / 12 = 0.5 (option C), jo ek medium-size effect mana jaata hai. Trap: option A ratio ulta leta hai (12 / 6); option B sirf raw farq hai, standardise nahi kiya; option D ek decimal galat jagah lag gaya.

questions.question: Do sales training programmes: A me 36 reps, average monthly sales ₹520 (hazaar), s = 60; B me 25 reps, average ₹490, s = 50. Welch t-test (two-sided, α = 0.05; df ≈ 56 pe t critical 2.003) ka result kya hai?
options: t ≈ 2.12, H₀ reject
t = 1.50, H₀ reject nahi
t ≈ 15.7, H₀ reject
t ≈ 2.12, H₀ reject nahi
questions.explanation: v_A = 60² / 36 = 100, v_B = 50² / 25 = 100. SE = √(100 + 100) ≈ 14.14, t = (520 − 490) / 14.14 ≈ 2.12 > 2.003, toh H₀ reject: option A. Trap: option B SEs ko jod deta hai (10 + 10 = 20) jabki variances jodte hain; option C s ko square kiye bina n se divide karta hai; option D sahi t pe galat decision leta hai.

questions.question: 3 discount levels ke ANOVA me SSB = 48 aur SSW = 152 aaye. η² kya hai, aur iska matlab kya hai?
options: 0.24; sales ke variation ka 24% discount level se explain hota hai
0.316; sales ke variation ka 31.6% discount level se explain hota hai
0.76; sales ke variation ka 76% discount level se explain hota hai
4.26; discount ka effect 4.26 guna hai
questions.explanation: SST = SSB + SSW = 48 + 152 = 200, η² = SSB / SST = 48 / 200 = 0.24: option A. Trap: option B SSB / SSW leta hai (denominator galat); option C within-group share (152 / 200) hai, jo unexplained hissa hai; option D F-statistic jaisa number hai, effect size nahi.

questions.question: Ek checkout A/B test: A me 4,000 visitors se 200 orders, B me 4,000 visitors se 248 orders. Pooled two-proportion z-test (two-sided, α = 0.05, critical 1.96) ka result aur lift kya hai?
options: z ≈ 2.33; significant; lift 24 percentage points
z ≈ 2.33; significant; lift 1.2 pp, yaani 24% relative
z ≈ 1.65; significant nahi; lift 1.2 pp
z ≈ 2.33; significant nahi, kyunki lift sirf 1.2 pp hai
questions.explanation: p̂_A = 5%, p̂_B = 6.2%. Pooled p̂ = 448 / 8,000 = 0.056, SE = √(0.056 × 0.944 × (1/4,000 + 1/4,000)) ≈ 0.00514, z = 0.012 / 0.00514 ≈ 2.33 > 1.96, toh significant. Lift = 1.2 pp, relative 1.2 / 5 = 24%: option B. Trap: option A relative lift ko pp bol deta hai; option D chhote absolute lift ko significance ke against maan leta hai (significance z se tay hoti hai); option C ka z galat hai.

questions.question: 3 packaging designs, har design 5 stores me (N = 15). Weekly units ke group means 20, 24, 28 hain aur har group ki SD 4 hai. One-way ANOVA (F(2, 12) ka 5% critical 3.885) ka F, decision aur η² kya hai?
options: F = 1.0, H₀ reject nahi
F = 5.0, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 0.83
F = 5.0, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 0.45
F ≈ 5.83, H₀ reject; η² ≈ 0.45
questions.explanation: Grand mean 24. SSB = 5 × ((20 − 24)² + 0 + (28 − 24)²) = 5 × 32 = 160, MSB = 160 / 2 = 80. SSW = 3 × (5 − 1) × 4² = 192, MSW = 192 / 12 = 16. F = 80 / 16 = 5.0 > 3.885, reject. η² = 160 / (160 + 192) ≈ 0.45: option C. Trap: option A SSB me group size 5 se multiply karna bhool jaata hai (SSB = 32); option B η² = SSB / SSW leta hai; option D MSW ke liye N − 1 = 14 se divide karta hai, N − k = 12 se nahi.

questions.question: 4 delivery partners ka ANOVA significant aaya. Saare pairwise tests ke p-values: 0.004, 0.012, 0.030, 0.0009, 0.20, 0.06. Family-wise α = 0.05 pe Bonferroni correction ke baad kitne pairs significantly alag hain?
options: 4 pairs
3 pairs
1 pair
2 pairs
questions.explanation: 4 groups ⇒ m = 4 × 3 / 2 = 6 pairs, har test 0.05 / 6 ≈ 0.0083 pe. Sirf 0.004 aur 0.0009 isse chhote hain, toh 2 pairs: option D. Trap: option A bina correction 0.05 se compare karta hai; option B m = 4 (groups ki sankhya) se divide karta hai (0.0125, jisse 0.012 bhi pass ho jaata); option C sirf sabse chhota p-value ginta hai.

questions.question: Do warehouse layouts ka picking time: Layout A: n = 40, mean 50 sec, s = 5. Layout B: n = 10, mean 44 sec, s = 15. Pooled t ≈ 2.15 aata hai (df = 48 pe critical 2.011). Welch test ke saath (df ≈ 9.5; df = 9 pe critical 2.262) sahi report kya hai?
options: Pooled t ≈ 2.15 report karo: significant, kyunki total n = 50 hai
Welch t ≈ 1.25, significant nahi; SDs 5 vs 15 bahut alag hain
Welch t ≈ 2.15, significant, kyunki dono tests same t dete hain
Welch t ≈ 1.25, significant, kyunki 1.25 > 1
questions.explanation: Welch: v_A = 5² / 40 = 0.625, v_B = 15² / 10 = 22.5, SE = √23.125 ≈ 4.81, t = 6 / 4.81 ≈ 1.25 < 2.262, toh significant nahi: option B. Pooled t galat hai kyunki SD ratio 15 / 5 = 3 > 2 aur sizes bhi bahut alag hain; pooled variance chhote, noisy group B ko kam aankti hai. Trap: option A bade total n se pooled ko sahi maan leta hai; option C maan leta hai ki dono tests ka t same hota hai; option D t ko critical value ki jagah 1 se compare karta hai.

weeks.title: Explaining stock-like returns with simple and multiple regression
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki stock returns ko market model (beta) se kaise explain karte hain, multiple regression me har coefficient ko 'baaki sab constant' rakh ke kaise padhte hain, coefficients pe t-test aur confidence interval kaise lagate hain, adjusted R² kyun chahiye, aur ek variable chhod dene se baaki coefficients kaise biased ho jaate hain.
concepts: **Prices nahi, returns**: return rₜ = (Pₜ − Pₜ₋₁) / Pₜ₋₁. Prices time ke saath trend karte hain, isliye do trending price series ko regress karne pe bina kisi asli rishte ke bhi bada R² aa jaata hai (**spurious regression**). Returns ka mean aur spread zyada stable hota hai, isliye analysis returns pe karte hain.

**Market model**: Rᵢ = α + β·R_m + ε. Slope **β = Cov(Rᵢ, R_m) / Var(R_m)** batata hai ki market 1 percentage point hile toh stock average kitna hilta hai: β > 1 aggressive, β < 1 defensive. R² = stock ke variance ka market-explained (systematic) hissa; 1 − R² company-specific (idiosyncratic) risk hai jo diversification se ghatta hai.

**Multiple regression**: ŷ = b₀ + b₁x₁ + … + b_k x_k, OLS SSE = Σ(y − ŷ)² minimise karta hai; matrix form me b = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy. Har bⱼ ek **partial effect** hai: xⱼ 1 unit badhe aur baaki predictors constant rahein toh predicted y me average change. Yeh simple regression ke slope se alag ho sakta hai, kyunki ab doosre variables ka asar alag kar diya gaya hai.

**Coefficients pe inference**: t = bⱼ / SE(bⱼ), df = n − k − 1 (k = predictors). 95% CI = bⱼ ± t* × SE(bⱼ). 'β = 1 hai kya?' jaise sawaal ke liye t = (b − 1) / SE lo; default regression output hamesha H₀: β = 0 test karta hai.

**R² vs adjusted R²**: naya variable jodne pe R² kabhi nahi ghatta, chahe variable bekaar ho. **Adjusted R² = 1 − (1 − R²)(n − 1) / (n − k − 1)** extra predictors ki penalty lagata hai, isliye alag size ke models compare karne ke liye yeh behtar hai. Overall F-test (H₀: saare slopes 0): F = (R² / k) / ((1 − R²) / (n − k − 1)).

**Omitted variable bias (OVB)**: agar asli model y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + ε hai par x₂ chhod diya, toh x₁ ka simple slope average me β₁ + β₂·δ deta hai, jahan δ = x₂ ko x₁ pe regress karne ka slope. Bias tab hota hai jab chhoda gaya variable y ko affect kare (β₂ ≠ 0) aur x₁ se correlated ho (δ ≠ 0).

**Explain vs predict**: in-sample R² ko prediction power mat samjho. Returns me out-of-sample R² aksar bahut chhota hota hai; model ko time-ordered train/test split pe check karo (pehle ke months pe fit, baad ke months pe test). Coefficients ke units hamesha likho: 'per 1 percentage point market return', 'per ₹1 crore ad spend'.

example.problem: Nilgiri Motors (fictional) aur market index ke 6 monthly returns (%): R_m = 2, −1, 3, 0, 4, −2; Rᵢ = 6, −3, 3, −3, 5, −2. Market model ka β, α aur R² nikaalo, aur market +2% hone pe expected stock return batao.
steps: R² = Sxy² / (Sxx × Syy) = 1764 / 2408 ≈ 0.73: stock ke return variance ka lagbhag 73% market se explain hota hai (toy data; asli monthly data me aksar kaafi kam hota hai).
**Answer**: **β = 1.5** (aggressive stock), **α = −0.5%**, **R² ≈ 0.73**, aur market +2% pe expected return **2.5%**.
example.code:
rm = [2, -1, 3, 0, 4, -2]
ri = [6, -3, 3, -3, 5, -2]
n = len(rm)
mx, my = sum(rm) / n, sum(ri) / n
sxx = sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in rm)
sxy = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(rm, ri))
syy = sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ri)
beta = sxy / sxx
alpha = my - beta * mx
print(beta, alpha, round(sxy ** 2 / (sxx * syy), 3))   # 1.5 -0.5 0.733

mistakes: Multiple regression ke coefficient ko simple correlation ki tarah padhna. Fix: har coefficient 'baaki predictors constant' wala partial effect hai; doosre variable jodne pe uski value badal sakti hai.
R² badhne ko model behtar hone ka saboot maanna. Fix: adjusted R² aur out-of-sample error dekho; bekaar variable bhi R² thoda badha deta hai.
Default t-test (H₀: β = 0) ko 'β = 1' wale sawaal ke liye use karna. Fix: jis value ke against test karna hai woh numerator me ghatao: t = (b − 1) / SE.
revision: Returns pe regression, prices pe nahi (spurious regression).
β = Cov(Rᵢ, R_m) / Var(R_m); R² = systematic risk ka share.
bⱼ = partial effect, baaki predictors constant.
t = b / SE, df = n − k − 1; CI = b ± t* × SE.
OVB: simple slope ≈ β₁ + β₂·δ.

questions.question: Ek stock ka market model R̂ᵢ = 0.2 + 1.3·R_m hai (dono % me). Agar agle mahine market return 2% ho, toh stock ka expected return kya hai?
questions.explanation: R̂ᵢ = 0.2 + 1.3 × 2 = 0.2 + 2.6 = 2.8%, option B. Trap: option A intercept bhool jaata hai (sirf 1.3 × 2); option C β ko multiply karne ki jagah jod deta hai (0.2 + 1.3 + 2); option D market return lagana hi bhool jaata hai (0.2 + 1.3).

questions.question: Ek bank stock ke monthly returns pe model: R̂ = 0.5 + 1.1·Market − 0.4·RateChange, jahan Market = market return (%) aur RateChange = policy rate me change (percentage points). −0.4 ka sahi interpretation kya hai?
options: Market return constant rehte hue, policy rate 1 percentage point badhne pe stock ka predicted return average 0.4 percentage point kam hota hai
Policy rate badhne se stock ka return hamesha 0.4% girta hai, market chahe kuch bhi kare
Stock return aur rate change ka correlation −0.4 hai
Policy rate 1 percentage point badhne pe stock ka return 40% girta hai
questions.explanation: Multiple regression ka coefficient partial effect hai: Market ko fixed rakh ke RateChange me 1 unit (1 pp) badhne pe predicted return me average −0.4 pp change, isliye option A. Trap: option C coefficient ko correlation samajh leta hai (slope aur correlation alag cheezein hain); option B 'average' aur 'baaki constant' dono shart hata deta hai; option D units galat padhta hai.

questions.question: 30 months ke data pe 3 predictors wala return model fit hua aur R² = 0.64 aaya. Adjusted R² kya hai?
questions.explanation: Adj R² = 1 − (1 − 0.64)(30 − 1) / (30 − 3 − 1) = 1 − 0.36 × 29 / 26 = 1 − 0.4015 ≈ 0.598, option D. Trap: option B denominator me n − k = 27 leta hai (intercept ka df bhool gaye); option C numerator me n = 30 leta hai (n − 1 ki jagah); option A penalty lagata hi nahi.

questions.question: 40 observations aur 2 predictors wale model me ek coefficient b = 0.85, SE = 0.30 hai. df = 37 pe two-sided 5% t critical = 2.026. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: t ≈ 0.35; coefficient significant nahi
t ≈ 2.83; significant (H₀: β = 0 reject); 95% CI ≈ (0.24, 1.46)
t ≈ 2.83; significant nahi, kyunki 95% CI me 1 aata hai
questions.explanation: t = 0.85 / 0.30 ≈ 2.83 > 2.026 ⇒ H₀: β = 0 reject. CI = 0.85 ± 2.026 × 0.30 = 0.85 ± 0.608 ≈ (0.24, 1.46), option C. Trap: option D 'CI me 1' ko 'CI me 0' samajh leta hai; CI me 1 hone ka matlab sirf itna hai ki β = 1 reject nahi hota. Option B t* se multiply karna bhool jaata hai, aur option A SE / b leta hai.

questions.question: Ek stock ke monthly returns ke liye: Cov(Rᵢ, R_m) = 18, Var(R_m) = 12, Var(Rᵢ) = 45 (units: %²). Market model ka β aur R² kya hai?
questions.explanation: β = Cov / Var(R_m) = 18 / 12 = 1.5. r = 18 / √(12 × 45) = 18 / 23.24 ≈ 0.775, aur R² = r² = 324 / 540 = 0.6, isliye option D. Trap: option B r ko hi R² maan leta hai (square karna bhool gaye); option A stock ka variance divide karta hai (18 / 45); option C ratio ulta leta hai (12 / 18).

questions.question: Ek auto stock ka asli model hai: R = 0.2 + 0.5·Market + 1.5·Sector + ε, jahan Sector = auto-sector index ka return. Sector ko Market pe regress karne pe slope 0.4 aata hai. Agar analyst Sector ko chhod ke sirf R ko Market pe regress kare, toh Market ka slope average me kitna aayega?
questions.explanation: Omitted variable bias: simple slope = β_Market + β_Sector × δ = 0.5 + 1.5 × 0.4 = 1.1, option B. Market ka slope sector ka asar bhi 'utha' leta hai kyunki dono correlated hain. Trap: option A maan leta hai ki variable chhodne se kuch nahi badalta; option C dono coefficients jod deta hai; option D δ ko seedha jod deta hai (0.5 + 0.4), β_Sector se multiply kiye bina.

questions.question: Ek intern do companies ke 10 saal ke daily **share prices** ko ek doosre pe regress karta hai aur R² = 0.92 aata hai. Senior analyst kehta hai ki yeh result bharose layak nahi. Sabse sahi wajah kya hai?
options: Prices pe R² hamesha 1 ke paas hota hai, isliye 0.92 kam hai
Dono series trend karti hain; asli rishte ke bina bhi R² bada aata hai
10 saal ka daily data regression ke liye bahut kam hai
Regression sirf positive numbers pe kaam karta hai, prices pe nahi
questions.explanation: Trending price series ko regress karne pe common trend ki wajah se bada R² aa jaata hai, chahe asli rishta na ho (spurious regression); isliye returns pe analysis karte hain: option B. Trap: option C sun ke sahi lagta hai par 10 saal ka daily data kaafi bada hai; options A aur D regression ke baare me galat facts hain.

questions.question: Ek FMCG stock ka market model R̂ᵢ = 0 + 0.7·R_m hai (dono % me). Agar market ek mahine me 4% gire, toh stock ka expected return kya hai?
questions.explanation: R̂ᵢ = 0.7 × (−4) = −2.8% (option A). β = 0.7 < 1 hai, toh stock defensive hai aur market se kam girta hai. Trap: option C 4 / 0.7 jaisa divide kar deta hai; option B 4 + 0.7 jodta hai, aur option D sign bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek pharma stock ke market model ka R² = 0.35 hai. Iska sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Stock aur market returns ka correlation 0.35 hai
Stock ka β 0.35 hai, yaani defensive stock
Variance ka 35% market se, 65% company-specific hai
Stock har mahine market se 35% zyada return deta hai
questions.explanation: R² = stock ke return variance ka market-explained (systematic) hissa = 35%; baaki 1 − 0.35 = 65% idiosyncratic hai jo diversification se ghat sakta hai: option C. Trap: option A R² ko r maan leta hai (yahan r = √0.35 ≈ 0.59); option B R² aur β ko mix karta hai, jo alag cheezein hain; option D return level ki baat hai, variance ki nahi.

questions.question: 60 monthly returns pe market model me b = 1.4 aur SE(b) = 0.16 aaya (df = 58 pe two-sided 5% t critical ≈ 2.002). Kya stock ka β significantly 1 se alag hai?
options: t = 8.75; haan, β = 1 clearly reject hota hai
t = 2.5; nahi, kyunki 1.4 aur 1 ka farq chhota hai
t = 0.4; nahi, β = 1 reject nahi hota hai
t = 2.5; haan, β = 1 reject, stock aggressive hai
questions.explanation: H₀: β = 1, toh t = (b − 1) / SE = (1.4 − 1) / 0.16 = 2.5 > 2.002: reject, aur b > 1 hai toh stock aggressive hai: option D. Trap: option A default output wala t = 1.4 / 0.16 = 8.75 hai, jo H₀: β = 0 test karta hai; option C SE se divide karna bhool jaata hai (1.4 − 1 = 0.4); option B sahi t pe galat decision leta hai.

questions.question: 25 quarters ke data pe 4 predictors wala sales model fit hua aur R² = 0.50 aaya. Overall F-statistic (H₀: saare slopes 0) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F = (R² / k) / ((1 − R²) / (n − k − 1)) = (0.50 / 4) / (0.50 / 20) = 0.125 / 0.025 = 5.0 (option A). Trap: option B sirf R² / (1 − R²) hai, degrees of freedom bhool gaya; option C denominator me n − 1 = 24 leta hai; option D numerator me k + 1 = 5 se divide karta hai.

questions.question: Kaveri Textiles (fictional) aur market ke 5 monthly returns (%): R_m = 2, 0, −1, 3, 1; Rᵢ = 2.5, 0.5, −1.5, 1.5, −0.5. Market model ka β, α aur R² kya hai?
questions.explanation: Means: R̄_m = 1, R̄ᵢ = 0.5. Market deviations 1, −1, −2, 2, 0 ⇒ Sxx = 10; stock deviations 2, 0, −2, 1, −1 ⇒ Sxy = 2 + 0 + 4 + 2 + 0 = 8, Syy = 10. β = 8 / 10 = 0.8, α = 0.5 − 0.8 × 1 = −0.3, R² = 8² / (10 × 10) = 0.64: option C. Trap: option D r = 0.8 ko R² bol deta hai; option B α ko sirf stock ka mean maan leta hai; option A β = Sxx / Sxy ulta leta hai.

questions.question: Ek analyst ne weekly sales ko sirf ad spend pe regress kiya aur slope 1.8 aaya. Asli model me store footfall bhi hai, jiska coefficient 0.6 hai, aur footfall ko ad spend pe regress karne pe slope 0.5 aata hai. Ad spend ka asli partial effect (footfall constant) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: OVB: simple slope = β₁ + β₂ · δ, toh 1.8 = β₁ + 0.6 × 0.5 = β₁ + 0.3, isliye β₁ = 1.5 (option D). Simple slope upward biased tha kyunki footfall sales badhata hai (β₂ > 0) aur ad spend ke saath badhta hai (δ > 0). Trap: option A bias ko ghatane ki jagah jod deta hai; option B simple slope ko hi partial effect maan leta hai; option C 1.8 × 0.5 karta hai, jiska koi matlab nahi.

questions.question: 31 months ke data pe do models: Model 1 (2 predictors) R² = 0.60; Model 2 (6 predictors) R² = 0.63. Adjusted R² ke hisaab se kaunsa model behtar hai?
options: Model 1: adjusted R² ≈ 0.571 vs 0.538
Model 2: R² 0.63 > 0.60, toh woh behtar hai
Model 2: 4 extra predictors ne R² 3 points badhaya
Dono barabar: adjusted R² dono ka ≈ 0.55 hai
questions.explanation: Adjusted R² = 1 − (1 − R²)(n − 1) / (n − k − 1). Model 1: 1 − 0.40 × 30 / 28 ≈ 0.571. Model 2: 1 − 0.37 × 30 / 24 ≈ 0.538. Model 1 aage hai: option A. Trap: options B aur C plain R² dekhte hain, jo naya variable jodne pe kabhi nahi ghatta, chahe variable bekaar ho; option D galat arithmetic hai.

questions.question: Ek cement stock ke monthly returns ka SD 8% hai, market ka SD 4% hai, aur dono ka correlation r = 0.6 hai. Market model ka β, R², aur diversifiable (idiosyncratic) variance ka share kya hai?
options: β = 0.3, R² = 0.36; 64% variance diversifiable
β = 1.2, R² = 0.36; 64% variance diversifiable
β = 1.2, R² = 0.6; 40% variance diversifiable
β = 2.0, R² = 0.36; 36% variance diversifiable
questions.explanation: β = Cov / Var(R_m) = r × σᵢ / σ_m = 0.6 × 8 / 4 = 1.2. R² = r² = 0.36, toh idiosyncratic share = 1 − 0.36 = 64%: option B. Trap: option A SDs ka ratio ulta leta hai (0.6 × 4 / 8); option C r ko hi R² maan leta hai; option D correlation ko ignore karke sirf σᵢ / σ_m leta hai aur systematic share ko diversifiable bol deta hai.

weeks.title: Regression diagnostics: residuals, collinearity and influential points
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki regression fit karne ke baad residual plots se non-linearity, heteroscedasticity aur autocorrelation kaise pakadte hain, VIF se multicollinearity kaise naapte hain, aur outliers, high-leverage points aur influential points (Cook's distance) me kya farq hai.
concepts: **Residual vs fitted plot** pehla diagnostic hai. Achhe model me residuals zero ke aas-paas random cloud jaise hote hain. **Curve** (U ya ∩ shape) ⇒ relation non-linear hai: x², log(x) ya alag functional form try karo. **Funnel** (fitted value badhne ke saath spread badhta hai) ⇒ heteroscedasticity.

**Heteroscedasticity**: error variance constant nahi hai, jaise bade stores ki sales me error bhi bada. Coefficients unbiased rehte hain, par unke standard errors (aur isliye t-tests, CIs) galat ho jaate hain. Remedies: y ka log lena (multiplicative relation ke liye natural), weighted least squares, ya heteroscedasticity-robust (White) standard errors.

**Independence aur Durbin–Watson**: time-ordered data me residuals aksar correlated hote hain (ek mahine ki galti agle mahine bhi). DW = Σ(eₜ − eₜ₋₁)² / Σeₜ², range 0–4: lagbhag 2 ⇒ no first-order autocorrelation, 2 se kaafi kam ⇒ positive autocorrelation, 2 se kaafi zyada ⇒ negative. Normality ko normal Q-Q plot se check karo; bade n me yeh sabse kam critical assumption hai.

**Multicollinearity**: predictors aapas me strongly correlated (jaise TV spend aur total media spend). Symptoms: overall F aur R² high, par individual t-tests insignificant; coefficients ke sign ulte ya data thoda badalne pe bahut hilte hain. Predictions theek reh sakti hain; problem coefficients ke interpretation me hai.

**VIF (variance inflation factor)**: VIFⱼ = 1 / (1 − Rⱼ²), jahan Rⱼ² = xⱼ ko baaki predictors pe regress karne ka R². SE(bⱼ) √VIFⱼ guna inflate hota hai. Rule of thumb: VIF > 5 dhyan do, > 10 serious. Remedies: ek variable hatao, variables combine karo (index / ratio), ya zyada data lao.

**Outlier vs leverage**: outlier ka y apne predicted value se door hai (bada residual; standardised residual |r| > 2 ya 3). **Leverage** hᵢᵢ batata hai ki point x-space me kitna door hai; simple regression me hᵢᵢ = 1/n + (xᵢ − x̄)² / Sxx. Average leverage p / n hota hai (p = parameters including intercept); hᵢᵢ > 2p / n high maana jaata hai.

**Influence aur Cook's distance**: influential point woh hai jise hatane se fitted line kaafi badal jaaye. Cook's Dᵢ = (eᵢ² / (p·MSE)) × hᵢᵢ / (1 − hᵢᵢ)², yaani residual aur leverage dono milke. Ek high-leverage point line ko apni taraf kheench leta hai, isliye uska residual chhota dikh sakta hai; isliye sirf residuals dekh ke influential points nahi pakde jaate. Dᵢ > 1 (ya 4 / n se bahut bada) ho toh investigate karo: data error hai, ya alag regime (jaise long-distance flat pricing)?

example.problem: Ek delivery startup (fictional) ka cost (₹) vs distance (km): x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 15; y = 30, 38, 44, 52, 58, 75. Saare points ke saath aur 15 km wale point ke bina slope nikaalo, aur 15 km point ka leverage aur Cook's D batao.
steps: Saare 6 points: x̄ = 5, ȳ = 49.5, Sxx = 130, Sxy = 376 ⇒ slope = 376 / 130 ≈ 2.89, intercept ≈ 35.04.
15 km point ka leverage: h = 1/6 + (15 − 5)² / 130 = 0.167 + 0.769 ≈ 0.94; threshold 2p / n = 2 × 2 / 6 ≈ 0.67, toh bahut high leverage.
Uska residual = 75 − (35.04 + 2.89 × 15) ≈ −3.42, jo baaki residuals (−7.9 se 8.5) se chhota hai: line khud is point ki taraf khinch gayi hai.
Point hatane pe (pehle 5 points): x̄ = 3, Sxx = 10, Sxy = 70 ⇒ slope = 7.0, intercept 23.4.
Interpretation: short distances pe cost ≈ ₹7 per km badhta hai, par 15 km order lagbhag flat-rate jaisa hai. Ek hi model dono regimes ko mix karke misleading slope de raha tha.

**Answer**: slope **2.89 (saare points) vs 7.0 (bina 15 km)**; 15 km point ka **h ≈ 0.94** aur **Cook's D ≈ 29**, yaani highly influential; ise alag pricing regime ki tarah model karo, chupchaap delete mat karo.

mistakes: Sirf bade residuals dhoond ke influential points pakadne ki koshish. Fix: leverage aur Cook's D bhi dekho; high-leverage point ka residual chhota hi dikhta hai kyunki line uski taraf khinchi hoti hai.

Insignificant t-tests dekh ke 'in variables ka koi asar nahi' bolna jab VIF bahut high ho. Fix: collinear variables ka joint F-test karo ya unhe combine karo; individual t sirf unique contribution test karta hai.
Outlier ko automatically delete karna. Fix: pehle check karo ki data error hai ya asli alag behaviour; delete kiya toh report me likho aur dono results dikhao.
revision: Curve ⇒ non-linear; funnel ⇒ heteroscedasticity (SEs galat).
DW ≈ 2 theek; < 2 positive autocorrelation.
VIF = 1 / (1 − Rⱼ²); SE √VIF guna badhta hai.
Leverage h = 1/n + (x − x̄)² / Sxx; high agar > 2p / n.
Cook's D = residual + leverage; D > 1 investigate.

questions.question: Store-level sales regression ke residual vs fitted plot me residuals zero ke aas-paas hain, par fitted value badhne ke saath unka spread funnel ki tarah failta jaata hai. Yeh kis problem ka sign hai?
options: Multicollinearity
Non-linearity
Heteroscedasticity
Perfect fit
questions.explanation: Spread ka fitted value ke saath badhna non-constant error variance, yaani heteroscedasticity hai, option C; isse SEs aur t-tests unreliable ho jaate hain (fix: log y, WLS ya robust SE). Trap: option B ka sign curve/U-shape hota hai, funnel nahi; option A predictors ke aapas ke correlation ki problem hai jo residual plot ki shape se nahi dikhti.

questions.question: Ek demand model me 'digital ad spend' ko baaki predictors pe regress karne pe R² = 0.8 aata hai. Digital ad spend ka VIF kya hai?
questions.explanation: VIF = 1 / (1 − Rⱼ²) = 1 / (1 − 0.8) = 1 / 0.2 = 5, option D. Trap: option A tolerance (1 − Rⱼ²) hai, VIF nahi; option B 1 / Rⱼ² le leta hai; option C sirf Rⱼ² hai.

questions.question: Simple regression me 5 cities ka data hai, x (population, lakh) = 2, 4, 6, 8, 30. x = 30 wali city ka leverage hᵢᵢ kya hai, aur 2p / n rule (p = 2) se kya woh high-leverage hai?
options: h ≈ 0.97; haan, kyunki 0.97 > 0.8
h ≈ 0.77; nahi, kyunki 0.77 < 0.8
h = 0.2; nahi, saare points ka leverage barabar hai
h ≈ 0.97; nahi, leverage sirf y ke bade residual se aata hai
questions.explanation: x̄ = 50 / 5 = 10, Sxx = 64 + 36 + 16 + 4 + 400 = 520. h = 1/5 + (30 − 10)² / 520 = 0.2 + 0.769 ≈ 0.97. Threshold 2p / n = 4 / 5 = 0.8, toh high leverage: option A. Trap: option B 1/n wala term bhool jaata hai; option C sirf 1/n leta hai; option D leverage ko residual se confuse karta hai, jabki leverage sirf x pe depend karta hai.

questions.question: Ek sales model me TV spend aur total media spend dono predictors hain (correlation 0.95). Overall F-test bahut significant hai aur R² = 0.85, par dono variables ke individual t-tests insignificant hain. Sabse sahi explanation kya hai?
options: Dono variables ka sales pe koi asar nahi hai, inhe hata do
Multicollinearity: dono ka information overlap karta hai, isliye individual SEs inflate ho gaye, jabki milke woh sales explain karte hain
Heteroscedasticity ki wajah se F-test galat hai
Model overfit hai kyunki R² 0.85 se zyada nahi hona chahiye
questions.explanation: Jab predictors highly correlated hon, model ko pata nahi chalta ki effect kis variable ko de; SEs (√VIF guna) badh jaate hain aur individual t chhote ho jaate hain, jabki joint F aur R² high rehte hain: option B. Trap: option A individual insignificance ko 'koi effect nahi' padhta hai; joint F-test saaf batata hai ki dono milke important hain. Option C ki koi evidence nahi di gayi.

questions.question: Ek predictor ka VIF = 9 hai. Agar woh predictor baaki predictors se uncorrelated hota (VIF = 1), uski tulna me uske coefficient ka standard error kitne guna hai?
options: 3 guna
9 guna
81 guna
1/9 guna (chhota)
questions.explanation: VIF variance ko inflate karta hai; SE variance ka square root hai, isliye SE √9 = 3 guna, option A. Trap: option B VIF ko seedha SE pe laga deta hai (9 variance ka factor hai); option C VIF ko square kar deta hai; option D direction ulti kar deta hai.

questions.question: Monthly sales regression ke 6 consecutive residuals hain: 2, 1, −1, −2, −1, 1. Durbin–Watson statistic kya hai aur woh kya batata hai?
options: ≈ 0.92; koi problem nahi, kyunki DW 0 aur 4 ke beech hai
≈ 0.92; negative autocorrelation
≈ 0.92; positive autocorrelation: residuals ke runs hain, independence assumption toot rahi hai
≈ 3.08; negative autocorrelation
questions.explanation: Differences: −1, −2, −1, 1, 2 ⇒ squares ka sum = 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 4 = 11. Σe² = 4 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 12. DW = 11 / 12 ≈ 0.92, jo 2 se kaafi kam hai ⇒ positive autocorrelation (residuals pehle positive, phir negative runs me): option C. Trap: option A sochta hai ki 0–4 range me hona hi theek hai, jabki ideal ~2 hai; option D 4 − DW le leta hai; option B direction ulti padhta hai.

questions.question: Ad spend vs sales regression ke residual vs fitted plot me residuals ek saaf **U-shape** banate hain: beech me negative, dono kinaron pe positive. Sabse sahi agla step kya hai?
options: Weighted least squares lagao, kyunki spread badh raha hai
Relation non-linear hai: x² ya log(x) jaisa functional form try karo
Kuch nahi, residuals ka average zero hai toh model theek hai
VIF check karo, kyunki yeh multicollinearity ka sign hai
questions.explanation: U ya ∩ pattern ka matlab hai ki straight line relation ko capture nahi kar rahi: non-linearity. Isliye x², log(x) jaisa form try karo (option B). Trap: option A funnel shape (heteroscedasticity) ka remedy hai, curve ka nahi; option C bhool jaata hai ki average zero hote hue bhi systematic pattern ho sakta hai; option D predictors ke aapsi correlation ki problem hai, jo residual plot me aise nahi dikhti.

questions.question: Ek store-sales regression me heteroscedasticity hai (bade stores me errors bade). Iska OLS results pe kya asar hota hai?
options: Coefficients biased ho jaate hain, par SEs sahi rehte hain
Model ka R² hamesha 1 ke paas pahunch jaata hai
Predictors aapas me correlated ho jaate hain
Coefficients unbiased rehte hain, par SEs aur t-tests galat hote hain
questions.explanation: Heteroscedasticity me OLS coefficients average me sahi (unbiased) rehte hain, par error variance constant maan ke nikle standard errors galat hote hain, isliye t-tests aur CIs pe bharosa nahi kar sakte: option D. Remedy: log(y), WLS ya robust (White) SEs. Trap: option A ulta bolta hai; option C multicollinearity hai, aur option B ka heteroscedasticity se koi rishta nahi.

questions.question: Monthly demand model ke residuals pe Durbin–Watson statistic 3.6 aaya. Iska kya matlab hai?
options: Negative autocorrelation: residuals baar-baar sign badalte hain
Positive autocorrelation: residuals ke lambe runs hain
Koi autocorrelation nahi, kyunki DW 0 aur 4 ke beech hai
Residuals normal distribution follow nahi karte
questions.explanation: DW ≈ 2 ka matlab no first-order autocorrelation; 2 se kaafi zyada (jaise 3.6) ka matlab negative autocorrelation, yaani ek positive residual ke baad aksar negative aata hai: option A. Trap: option B 2 se kam DW ka description hai; option C range ko hi test samajh leta hai (har DW 0–4 me hota hai); option D normality Q-Q plot se check hoti hai, DW se nahi.

questions.question: Ek pricing model me 'competitor price' ka VIF = 4 hai. Competitor price ko baaki predictors pe regress karne ka R² kya hai, aur uska SE kitne guna inflate hua hai?
options: R² = 0.25; SE 4 guna
R² = 0.75; SE 2 guna
R² = 0.75; SE 4 guna
R² = 0.80; SE 2 guna
questions.explanation: VIF = 1 / (1 − R²) = 4 ⇒ 1 − R² = 0.25 ⇒ R² = 0.75. SE √VIF guna inflate hota hai: √4 = 2: option B. Trap: option C variance inflation (4) ko SE inflation bol deta hai; option A 1 / VIF ko R² maan leta hai; option D ka R² 0.80 VIF = 5 deta, 4 nahi.

questions.question: 40 stores ke data pe 4 predictors + intercept wala regression (p = 5) hai. Chaar stores ke leverage values: 0.08, 0.22, 0.31, 0.12. 2p / n rule se kaunsa store high-leverage flag hoga?
options: Koi nahi, kyunki saare values 1 se kam hain
0.22 aur 0.31 dono, kyunki dono average 0.125 se upar hain
Sirf 0.08, kyunki uska leverage sabse kam hai
Sirf 0.31 wala, kyunki threshold 0.25 hai
questions.explanation: Average leverage = p / n = 5 / 40 = 0.125, aur high-leverage threshold 2p / n = 10 / 40 = 0.25. Sirf 0.31 isse upar hai: option D. Trap: option B average ko hi threshold maan leta hai, jisse 0.22 bhi flag ho jaata; option A leverage ki upper limit 1 ko rule samajhta hai; option C ulta padhta hai.

questions.question: Simple regression (p = 2) me ek point ka residual e = 6, leverage h = 0.5, aur model ka MSE = 9 hai. Is point ka Cook's distance kya hai, aur kya yeh investigate karna chahiye?
options: D = 4.0; haan, kyunki D > 1
D = 1.0; borderline, abhi chhod do
D = 2.0; haan, kyunki D > 1
D = 8.0; haan, kyunki D > 1
questions.explanation: Cook's D = (e² / (p · MSE)) × h / (1 − h)² = (36 / (2 × 9)) × 0.5 / 0.25 = 2 × 2 = 4.0, jo 1 se bahut bada hai: option A. Trap: option B (1 − h) ko square karna bhool jaata hai (2 × 0.5 = 1); option C sirf pehla factor hai, leverage wala hissa chhod diya; option D denominator me p bhool jaata hai (36 / 9 × 2).

questions.question: Ek courier (fictional) ka cost vs distance: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 10 km; y = ₹10, 14, 18, 22, 30. Saare points ke saath slope, 10 km wale point ke bina slope, aur us point ka leverage kya hai?
options: Slope 4.0 dono cases me; h ≈ 0.20
Slope 2.08 (saare) vs 4.0 (bina); h ≈ 0.92
Slope 2.08 (saare) vs 4.0 (bina); h ≈ 0.20, yaani normal point
Slope 4.0 (saare) vs 2.08 (bina); h ≈ 0.92
questions.explanation: Saare points: x̄ = 4, Sxx = 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 36 = 50, Sxy = 104 ⇒ slope = 2.08. Pehle 4 points perfect line pe hain (har km pe ₹4), toh bina 10 km point slope = 4.0. Leverage = 1/5 + (10 − 4)² / 50 = 0.2 + 0.72 = 0.92 > 2p / n = 0.8: option B. Point ka residual sirf ≈ −1.28 hai kyunki line uski taraf khinch gayi. Trap: option C leverage me sirf 1/n leta hai; option D slopes ulte likhta hai; option A maan leta hai ki ek point slope nahi hila sakta.

questions.question: Ek model me sirf do predictors hain: store area aur number of checkout counters, aur dono ka correlation 0.9 hai. Har predictor ka VIF, aur uske SE ka inflation factor kya hai?
options: VIF = 0.81; SE 0.9 guna
VIF = 10; SE √10 ≈ 3.16 guna
VIF ≈ 5.26; SE 5.26 guna
VIF ≈ 5.26; SE ≈ 2.29 guna
questions.explanation: Do predictors me ek ko doosre pe regress karne ka R² = r² = 0.81. VIF = 1 / (1 − 0.81) = 1 / 0.19 ≈ 5.26 (yaani 'dhyan do' zone). SE inflation = √5.26 ≈ 2.29: option D. Trap: option C VIF ko hi SE factor maan leta hai; option B r = 0.9 se seedha 1 / (1 − 0.9) = 10 nikaal leta hai, r ko square kiye bina; option A r² ko hi VIF bol deta hai.
