questions.question: 20 observations, simple regression (p = 2, toh 2p / n = 0.2). Chaar points ke diagnostics neeche hain. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: P sabse influential hai, kyunki uska residual sabse bada hai
Q sabse influential hai, kyunki uska leverage sabse zyada hai
R sabse influential hai: bada residual + high leverage, D > 1
Koi point influential nahi, kyunki saare |residual| 4 se kam hain
questions.explanation: Influence residual aur leverage dono ka combination hai. R ka |residual| 2.2 aur leverage 0.38 > 0.2, dono milke Cook's D = 1.48 > 1: option C. P outlier hai (|r| > 3) par low leverage (0.06) hone se line ko zyada nahi hilaata (D = 0.31); Q x-space me door hai par line ke kareeb baitha hai (D = 0.07). Trap: options A aur B sirf ek hi ingredient dekhte hain; option D outlier rule ko influence ka rule bana deta hai.

weeks.title: Pay analytics: dummy variables, interactions and mediation
weeks.summary: Is week aap ek faculty-salary case ke through seekhoge ki categorical predictors ko dummy variables se regression me kaise daalte hain, reference category aur dummy trap kya hain, interaction term se 'alag groups ke alag slopes' kaise model karte hain, aur mediation (X → M → Y) se direct aur indirect effect kaise alag karte hain.
concepts: **Case framing**: ek business school (fictional) pay-equity audit karna chahta hai: salary (₹ lakh / year) ko experience (years), rank (Assistant / Associate / Full professor), field aur gender se explain karna. Numeric predictors seedha jaate hain; categorical predictors ko pehle numbers me badalna padta hai.

**Dummy coding**: k categories wale variable ke liye **k − 1** dummies (0/1) banao; jo category chhoot jaati hai woh **reference category** hai. Rank ke liye Assoc = 1 agar Associate, Full = 1 agar Full; Assistant reference. Coefficient of Full = Full aur Assistant professors ki average salary ka farq, baaki predictors constant. Graph pe yeh parallel lines hain: dummy sirf intercept shift karta hai.

**Dummy variable trap**: intercept ke saath saari k dummies daal di toh Assist + Assoc + Full = 1 har row me, jo intercept column ke barabar hai: **perfect multicollinearity**, XᵀX invert nahi hota aur coefficients unique nahi rehte. Fix: ek dummy chhodo (ya intercept hatao).

**Reference badalna**: reference category badalne se coefficients badalte hain par predictions aur model fit bilkul same rehte hain. Do non-reference categories ka farq = unke coefficients ka difference (jaise Full − Assoc). Poore categorical variable ka effect test karna ho toh uske saare dummies pe ek saath partial F-test karo, individual t-tests pe nahi.

**Interaction (continuous × dummy)**: Salary = b₀ + b₁·Exp + b₂·Eng + b₃·(Exp × Eng). Non-Eng ka slope b₁, Eng ka slope b₁ + b₃; lines ab parallel nahi hain. b₂ sirf Exp = 0 pe gap hai, isliye kisi aur experience pe gap = b₂ + b₃·Exp. Interpretation aasaan karne ke liye Exp ko center karo (Exp − mean), taaki b₂ 'average experience pe gap' ban jaaye.

**Mediation (path idea)**: X → M → Y, jaise experience → publications → salary. Path a: M ko X pe regress karo; path b aur c′: Y ko X aur M dono pe regress karo. **Indirect effect = a × b**, **direct effect = c′**, aur linear OLS me total effect c = c′ + a·b. c′ ≈ 0 ho toh full mediation, warna partial. Indirect effect ka CI aajkal bootstrap se nikaalte hain.

**Bad controls**: mediator ko control karna galat sawaal ka answer de sakta hai. Agar gender promotion (rank) ko affect karta hai aur aap rank control karte ho, toh gender coefficient sirf 'same rank ke andar' gap dikhata hai, promotion wala gap chhup jaata hai. Pay-equity report me dono models (rank ke saath aur bina) dikhao, aur causal claims ke liye confounders ke baare me saaf assumptions likho.

example.problem: Deccan School of Business (fictional) ka fitted model: Salary = 12 + 0.6·Exp + 4·Assoc + 9·Full + 2.5·Finance (₹ lakh), jahan Assistant professor aur non-Finance field reference hain. (a) 10 saal experience wale Finance ke Associate professor, (b) 20 saal experience wale Marketing ke Full professor ki predicted salary nikaalo, aur (c) Full aur Associate ka gap batao.
steps: (a) Exp = 10, Assoc = 1, Full = 0, Finance = 1.
(b) Exp = 20, Assoc = 0, Full = 1, Finance = 0 (Marketing reference group me hai).
(c) Full − Associate = 9 − 4 = 5 lakh, same experience aur field pe; dono coefficients Assistant ke relative hain, isliye gap unka difference hai.
Dhyan do: Full professor ke liye Assoc = 0 hai; dummies cumulative nahi hote, ek row me rank ka sirf ek hi dummy (ya koi nahi) 1 hota hai.
**Answer**: (a) **₹24.5 lakh**, (b) **₹33 lakh**, (c) Full aur Associate ka gap **₹5 lakh**.

mistakes: Saari k categories ke dummies intercept ke saath daal dena. Fix: k − 1 dummies, aur report me reference category ka naam likho.
Interaction model me dummy ke coefficient ko 'har experience pe gap' padhna. Fix: gap = b₂ + b₃·Exp; b₂ sirf Exp = 0 pe gap hai.
Mediator (jaise rank) ko control karke 'gender gap nahi hai' conclude karna. Fix: total effect (bina mediator) aur direct effect (mediator ke saath) dono dikhao; farq indirect path hai.
revision: k categories ⇒ k − 1 dummies; coefficient = reference se farq.
Saari k dummies + intercept ⇒ perfect multicollinearity.
Reference badlo: coefficients badlenge, predictions nahi.
Interaction: Eng ka slope = b₁ + b₃; gap = b₂ + b₃·Exp.
Mediation: indirect = a × b, total = c′ + a·b.
Mediator ko control karna 'bad control' ban sakta hai.

questions.question: Ek salary regression me 'region' variable ki 4 categories hain (North, South, East, West), aur model me intercept hai. Region ke liye kitne dummy variables chahiye?
questions.explanation: k categories ke liye k − 1 = 4 − 1 = 3 dummies, aur chhooti hui region reference banti hai: option A. Trap: option B (4 dummies) intercept ke saath dummy variable trap (perfect multicollinearity) bana deta hai; option C region ko ek hi 1–4 coded number maan leta hai, jo regions ke beech fake ordering aur equal spacing thop deta hai.

questions.question: Faculty salary model (₹ lakh) me experience aur rank control karne ke baad Female dummy (1 = female, 0 = male) ka coefficient −1.2 hai. Iska sahi interpretation kya hai?
options: Female faculty ki salary male faculty se 1.2% kam hai
Same experience aur rank wale female faculty ki predicted salary male faculty se average ₹1.2 lakh kam hai
Har female faculty ki salary male se exactly ₹1.2 lakh kam hai
Gender aur salary ka correlation −1.2 hai
questions.explanation: Dummy coefficient reference group (male) ke relative average farq hai, model ke baaki predictors (experience, rank) constant rakh ke: option B. Trap: option A units galat padhta hai (y ₹ lakh me hai, log me nahi, isliye % nahi); option C 'average' hata ke har individual pe exact gap laga deta hai; option D coefficient ko correlation samajhta hai (correlation −1 se kam ho bhi nahi sakta).

questions.question: Model: Salary = 12 + 0.6·Exp + 4·Assoc + 9·Full + 2.5·Finance (₹ lakh); reference: Assistant professor, non-Finance field. 15 saal experience wale Finance ke Full professor ki predicted salary kya hai?
options: ₹20.5 lakh
₹36.5 lakh
₹32.5 lakh
₹30.0 lakh
questions.explanation: Full professor ke liye Full = 1, Assoc = 0, Finance = 1: 12 + 0.6 × 15 + 9 + 2.5 = 12 + 9 + 9 + 2.5 = 32.5, option C. Trap: option B Assoc ka 4 bhi jod deta hai, jaise rank dummies cumulative hon; option A intercept bhool jaata hai; option D Finance ka 2.5 chhod deta hai.

questions.question: Interaction model: Salary = 10 + 0.5·Exp + 3·Eng + 0.4·(Exp × Eng) (₹ lakh), jahan Eng = 1 engineering faculty ke liye. 10 saal experience pe Eng aur non-Eng faculty ki predicted salary me kitna gap hai, aur Eng ka experience slope kya hai?
options: Gap ₹3 lakh har experience level pe; Eng slope 0.5
Gap ₹3.4 lakh; Eng slope 0.4
Gap ₹7 lakh; dono groups ka slope 0.5
Gap ₹7 lakh; Eng ka slope 0.9 lakh per year
questions.explanation: Gap = b₂ + b₃·Exp = 3 + 0.4 × 10 = 7; Eng slope = b₁ + b₃ = 0.5 + 0.4 = 0.9, option D. Trap: option A b₂ = 3 ko har level ka gap maan leta hai, jabki interaction ki wajah se 3 sirf Exp = 0 pe gap hai; option B b₂ + b₃ jod deta hai bina Exp se multiply kiye; option C interaction ka slope pe asar bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek analyst intercept ke saath Assistant, Associate aur Full, teeno rank dummies model me daal deta hai. Software 'singular matrix' error deta hai. Iski wajah kya hai?
options: Sample size bahut chhota hai
Teeno dummies ka sum har row me 1 hai, jo intercept column ke barabar hai: perfect multicollinearity (dummy variable trap)
Rank aur salary me heteroscedasticity hai
Dummy variables regression me use hi nahi ho sakte
questions.explanation: Har faculty exactly ek rank me hai, toh Assist + Assoc + Full = 1 = intercept column. Ek column baaki columns ka exact linear combination hai, isliye XᵀX singular hai: option B. Fix: ek rank (jaise Assistant) chhodo. Trap: option A lagta hai, par bade sample me bhi yeh exact linear dependence wahi rahegi; option C ka matrix inversion se lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Mediation analysis (fictional data): Publications = 2 + 1.5·Exp (path a). Salary = 10 + 0.9·Exp + 0.6·Publications (path c′ aur b). Experience ka indirect effect, total effect, aur mediated proportion kya hai?
options: Indirect 0.6, total 1.5
Indirect 2.1, total 3.0
Indirect 0.9, total 1.8, lagbhag 50% effect publications ke through
Indirect 0.9, total 0.9: full mediation
questions.explanation: Indirect = a × b = 1.5 × 0.6 = 0.9 lakh per year; total = c′ + a·b = 0.9 + 0.9 = 1.8; mediated share = 0.9 / 1.8 = 50%, option C. Direct effect 0.9 abhi bhi non-zero hai, isliye yeh partial mediation hai. Trap: option D direct effect ko ignore karke full mediation bol deta hai; option B a aur b ko multiply karne ki jagah jod deta hai; option A sirf b ko indirect maan leta hai.

questions.question: Salary model (₹ lakh) me rank ke dummies hain aur Assistant professor reference category hai. Full dummy ka coefficient 9 hai. Iska sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Same experience aur field pe Full professors Assistant se average ₹9 lakh zyada kamaate hain
Full professors ki average salary ₹9 lakh hai
Full professors Associate professors se average ₹9 lakh zyada kamaate hain
Har Full professor ki salary har Assistant se exactly ₹9 lakh zyada hai
questions.explanation: Dummy ka coefficient hamesha reference category ke relative hota hai, baaki predictors constant rakhke: Full vs Assistant ka average gap ₹9 lakh (option A). Trap: option C reference galat category ko maan leta hai (Associate reference nahi hai); option B coefficient ko level samajh leta hai, gap nahi; option D average effect ko har individual pe exact laga deta hai.

questions.question: Model: Salary = b₀ + b₁·Exp + b₂·Female (koi interaction term nahi). Salary vs experience graph pe male aur female ki fitted lines kaisi dikhengi?
options: Ek hi line, kyunki slope same hai
Alag slopes wali lines jo kahin cross karti hain
Female line ka slope b₁ + b₂ hai
Parallel lines, jinke beech har experience pe gap b₂ hai
questions.explanation: Bina interaction ke dummy sirf intercept shift karta hai: dono groups ka slope b₁ hai, toh lines parallel hain aur har Exp pe vertical gap b₂ hai (option D). Trap: option B aur C interaction model (Exp × Female) ka description hain, jo is model me nahi hai; option A intercept shift ko bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek analyst rank ka reference category Assistant se badal ke Full professor kar deta hai, baaki model same. Kya badlega?
options: Har professor ki predicted salary badal jaayegi
Model ka R² aur fit dono behtar ho jaayenge
Dummy coefficients badlenge; predictions aur R² same
Kuch nahi badlega, coefficients bhi same rahenge
questions.explanation: Reference badalne se sirf comparison ka base badalta hai, isliye dummy coefficients (aur intercept) nayi values lete hain; par fitted values, residuals aur R² bilkul same rehte hain: option C. Trap: options A aur B maan lete hain ki model ka fit badla; option D bhool jaata hai ki coefficients ab Full ke relative hain, toh unki values badlengi.

questions.question: Ek sales-rep pay model me region dummies hain, West reference: North = 2.5, South = −1.0, East = 1.5 (₹ lakh). Same experience pe North aur South reps ki predicted pay me kitna gap hai?
options: ₹2.5 lakh
₹1.5 lakh
₹1.0 lakh
₹3.5 lakh
questions.explanation: Dono coefficients West ke relative hain, toh North − South = 2.5 − (−1.0) = ₹3.5 lakh (option D). Trap: option A North ka coefficient seedha gap maan leta hai, jo sirf North vs West hai; option C South ka sign bhool ke sirf |−1.0| leta hai; option B East ka coefficient hai, jo is sawaal se juda hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek company me women ko promotion kam milta hai. Pay audit me rank control karne pe gender coefficient lagbhag 0 aata hai, aur bina rank ke −3 lakh. Sabse sahi reading kya hai?
options: Same rank me gap nahi, par promotion se ₹3 lakh ka gap hai
Koi gender pay gap nahi hai, kyunki controlled model ka coefficient 0 hai
Bina rank wala model galat hai, use report nahi karna chahiye
Rank ek confounder hai, isliye sirf rank wala model sahi hai
questions.explanation: Rank yahan mediator hai (gender → promotion → salary). Use control karne se sirf 'same rank ke andar' wala gap bachta hai; −3 lakh ka total gap promotion path se aa raha hai. Isliye dono models dikhao: option A. Trap: option B bad control ka classic galat conclusion hai; options C aur D mediator ko confounder samajh ke total effect chhupa dete hain.

questions.question: Interaction model: Salary = 14 + 0.8·Exp − 4·Female + 0.2·(Exp × Female) (₹ lakh). 5 saal experience pe female − male gap kitna hai, aur kitne saal experience pe gap zero ho jaata hai?
options: Gap −4 lakh har experience pe; kabhi zero nahi hota
Gap −3 lakh; 5 saal pe hi zero
Gap −3 lakh; 20 saal pe zero
Gap −5 lakh; 20 saal pe zero
questions.explanation: Gap = b₂ + b₃·Exp = −4 + 0.2 × Exp. Exp = 5 pe −4 + 1 = −3 lakh. Zero tab jab 0.2 × Exp = 4, yaani Exp = 20: option C. Trap: option A interaction ko ignore karke b₂ ko har level ka gap maan leta hai; option D 0.2 × 5 ko ghata deta hai; option B gap aur crossover point ko mix karta hai.

questions.question: Model: Salary = 10 + 0.5·Exp + 3·Eng + 0.4·(Exp × Eng) (₹ lakh). Average experience 12 saal hai. Agar Exp ko center karke (Exp − 12) se model dobara fit karein, toh Eng dummy ka naya coefficient kya hoga?
options: 3.0, centering se dummy coefficient nahi badalta
questions.explanation: Centered model me Eng ka coefficient 'average experience (Exp = 12) pe gap' ban jaata hai: 3 + 0.4 × 12 = 3 + 4.8 = 7.8 (option D). Trap: option A sochta hai centering kuch nahi badalta, jo interaction model me galat hai (sirf bina interaction ke sahi hota); option C sirf 0.4 × 12 hai, b₂ bhool gaya; option B 3 + 0.4 hai, yaani Exp = 1 pe gap.

questions.question: Mediation (fictional): Salary ko sirf Exp pe regress karne pe slope (total effect) 2.4 hai. Publications = 3 + 2.0·Exp (path a), aur Salary ko Exp aur Publications dono pe regress karne pe Publications ka coefficient 0.5 hai (path b). Direct effect c′ aur mediated proportion kya hai?
options: c′ = 2.4, mediated 0%
c′ = 1.4, lagbhag 42% mediated
c′ = 3.4, lagbhag 29% mediated
c′ = 1.4, lagbhag 58% mediated
questions.explanation: Indirect = a × b = 2.0 × 0.5 = 1.0. Linear OLS me c = c′ + a·b, toh c′ = 2.4 − 1.0 = 1.4. Mediated proportion = 1.0 / 2.4 ≈ 42%: option B. Trap: option D direct effect ka share (1.4 / 2.4 ≈ 58%) hai, mediated share nahi; option C indirect ko ghatane ki jagah jodta hai; option A total ko hi direct maan leta hai.

questions.question: Model: Salary = 11 + 0.5·Exp + 3·Assoc + 7·Full + 2·Eng + 0.3·(Exp × Eng) (₹ lakh); reference Assistant aur non-Eng. 12 saal experience wale do log: Engineering ke Associate professor aur Marketing ke Full professor. Kiski predicted salary zyada hai, aur kitni?
options: Eng Associate ki, ₹1.6 lakh zyada
Marketing Full ki, ₹2.0 lakh zyada
Marketing Full ki, ₹1.4 lakh zyada
Dono ki barabar, ₹24 lakh
questions.explanation: Eng Associate: 11 + 0.5 × 12 + 3 + 2 + 0.3 × 12 = 11 + 6 + 3 + 2 + 3.6 = 25.6. Marketing Full: 11 + 6 + 7 = 24. Eng Associate ₹1.6 lakh aage hai: option A. Trap: option B interaction term (3.6) bhool jaata hai (Eng Associate = 22); option C Full ke liye Assoc dummy bhi 1 laga deta hai (11 + 6 + 3 + 7 = 27), jabki dummies cumulative nahi hote; option D sirf Full wala number dekhta hai.

weeks.title: Logistic regression for business classification decisions
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki churn ya loan default jaise yes/no outcomes ke liye logistic regression kyun use karte hain, odds, log-odds aur odds ratio ko kaise padhte hain, probability ko decision me badalne ke liye threshold kaise chunte hain, aur confusion matrix ke metrics (precision, recall, specificity) ko business cost ke saath kaise jodte hain.
concepts: **Linear regression kyun nahi**: outcome binary (churn = 1/0) ho toh linear model ki predictions 0 se kam ya 1 se zyada aa sakti hain, aur error variance p(1 − p) pe depend karta hai. Humein ek aisa model chahiye jo hamesha 0 aur 1 ke beech probability de.

**Logistic model**: log-odds linear hai: ln(p / (1 − p)) = β₀ + β₁x₁ + … + β_k x_k = z, aur p = 1 / (1 + e^(−z)). z = 0 ⇒ p = 0.5; z bada positive ⇒ p → 1; z bada negative ⇒ p → 0. Coefficients maximum likelihood se estimate hote hain (OLS se nahi); significance Wald z-test se, aur fit deviance / AIC se judge hota hai.

**Odds aur odds ratio**: odds = p / (1 − p); p = 0.2 ⇒ odds = 0.25 ('1 ke against 4'). xⱼ me 1 unit badhne pe odds **e^βⱼ** guna ho jaate hain (baaki constant). β = 0.693 ⇒ odds ratio ≈ 2, yaani odds double, probability double nahi. Probability pe asar baseline pe depend karta hai: p ≈ 0.5 ke paas sabse zyada (lagbhag β·p(1 − p) per unit), extremes pe kam.

**Probability se decision**: model probability deta hai; action ke liye threshold chahiye (p > t ⇒ 'churn hoga' predict karo). Default 0.5 sirf tab theek hai jab dono galtiyon ki cost barabar ho aur classes balanced hon.

**Confusion matrix**: TP (positive predict, sach me positive), FP (positive predict, asal me negative), FN (negative predict, asal me positive), TN. **Accuracy** = (TP + TN) / N; **precision** = TP / (TP + FP) ('jinhe flag kiya unme kitne sahi'); **recall / sensitivity** = TP / (TP + FN) ('asli positives me se kitne pakde'); **specificity** = TN / (TN + FP); F1 = precision aur recall ka harmonic mean.

**Class imbalance**: agar sirf 2% loans default hote hain, toh 'koi default nahi karega' bolne wala useless model bhi 98% accurate hai, par uska recall 0 hai. Rare-event problems me accuracy ki jagah precision, recall, aur cost-based evaluation dekho.

**Cost-based threshold**: agar FP ki cost C_FP aur FN ki cost C_FN hai, toh p > C_FP / (C_FP + C_FN) pe positive action lena expected cost minimise karta hai. **ROC curve** har threshold pe recall vs (1 − specificity) plot karta hai; **AUC** = random positive ko random negative se zyada score milne ki probability (0.5 = random, 1 = perfect ranking).

**Validation aur leakage**: model ko time-ordered holdout data pe check karo, aur probabilities calibrated hain ya nahi (predicted 20% wale group me sach me lagbhag 20% events). Outcome ke baad bani information (jaise 'collections team ka call hua') predictor me daal di toh test pe fake-good performance milegi: yeh **data leakage** hai.

example.problem: Sangam Telecom (fictional) ka churn model: ln(p / (1 − p)) = −2.0 + 0.8·Complaints − 0.05·Tenure, jahan Complaints = pichhle 3 mahine ki complaints, Tenure = months. Ek customer ki 3 complaints aur 12 months tenure hai. Churn probability, ek extra complaint ka odds ratio, aur kya ₹200 ka retention offer dena chahiye (customer value ₹3,000; offer churners me se 30% ko rok leta hai)?
steps: Ek extra complaint ⇒ odds × e^0.8 ≈ 2.23. 4 complaints pe p ≈ 0.646 ho jaata hai: probability 0.45 se 0.65 hui, double nahi hui, par odds 2.23 guna hue.
Offer ka expected benefit = P(churn) × value × save rate = 0.450 × 3,000 × 0.30 ≈ ₹405.
Expected benefit ₹405 > offer cost ₹200, toh is customer ko offer dena profitable hai (yeh maan ke ki offer sirf churners pe asar karta hai).
**Answer**: churn probability **≈ 0.45**, complaint ka **odds ratio ≈ 2.23**, aur offer **dena chahiye** (expected benefit ≈ ₹405 > ₹200).

mistakes: Odds ratio ko probability ka multiplier samajhna ('OR = 2 ⇒ churn probability double'). Fix: OR odds ko multiply karta hai; probability ka change baseline pe depend karta hai.
Imbalanced data pe sirf accuracy report karna. Fix: confusion matrix, precision, recall aur business cost dikhao; ek trivial 'sab negative' baseline se compare karo.
Hamesha 0.5 threshold use karna. Fix: FP aur FN ki cost se threshold tay karo, ya capacity (jaise 'collections team roz 200 calls kar sakti hai') ke hisaab se top-scored customers chuno.
revision: Odds = p / (1 − p); odds ratio = e^β per unit.
Precision = TP / (TP + FP); recall = TP / (TP + FN).
Specificity = TN / (TN + FP); rare events me accuracy misleading.
Cost threshold: p > C_FP / (C_FP + C_FN).
AUC = ranking quality; leakage se bacho.

questions.question: Ek credit model kehta hai ki ek applicant ke default karne ki probability 0.2 hai. Default ke odds kya hain?
questions.explanation: Odds = p / (1 − p) = 0.2 / 0.8 = 0.25, option D. Trap: option A probability ko hi odds maan leta hai; option C ratio ulta le leta hai (0.8 / 0.2 = 4, jo non-default ke odds hain); option B sirf 1 − p hai.

questions.question: Ek loan-default logistic model me 'pichhle 6 mahine me EMI miss ki' (dummy) ka coefficient 0.693 hai. Iska sahi interpretation kya hai?
options: Default ki probability 0.693 badh jaati hai
Default ki probability double ho jaati hai
Baaki variables constant rakh ke, default ke odds lagbhag 2 guna ho jaate hain
Default ke odds 69.3% badhte hain
questions.explanation: Odds ratio = e^0.693 ≈ 2.0, yaani EMI miss karne wale applicants ke default odds lagbhag double hain (baaki same), option C. Trap: option B odds ratio ko probability ratio samajh leta hai; probability ka change baseline pe depend karta hai. Option D β ko seedha % change maan leta hai (e^β nahi liya); option A coefficient ko probability ka change samajhta hai.

questions.question: Ek churn model: ln(p / (1 − p)) = −3 + 0.04·(monthly data usage in GB). 50 GB use karne wale customer ki churn probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: z = −3 + 0.04 × 50 = −1. p = 1 / (1 + e^1) = 1 / (1 + 2.718) ≈ 0.269, option B. Trap: option A sign galat leta hai (1 / (1 + e^(−1)) = 0.731, yaani z = +1 ki probability); option C log-odds ko hi probability maan leta hai (probability negative nahi ho sakti); option D e^(−1) hai, jo odds (0.368) hain, probability nahi.

questions.question: Ek fraud model ke 1,000 transactions ke test pe: TP = 80, FN = 20, FP = 120, TN = 780. Precision aur recall kya hain?
options: Precision 0.40, recall 0.80
Precision 0.80, recall 0.40
Precision 0.86, recall 0.80
Precision 0.40, recall 0.87
questions.explanation: Precision = TP / (TP + FP) = 80 / 200 = 0.40; recall = TP / (TP + FN) = 80 / 100 = 0.80, option A. Matlab model 80% frauds pakadta hai, par flag kiye gaye transactions me sirf 40% sach me fraud hain. Trap: option B dono formulas ulat deta hai; option C accuracy (860 / 1,000) ko precision maan leta hai; option D specificity (780 / 900 ≈ 0.87) ko recall maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek NBFC ke portfolio me sirf 2% loans default hote hain. Ek 'model' har applicant ko 'default nahi karega' predict karta hai. Is model ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Accuracy 98% hai, isliye yeh achha model hai
Accuracy 2% aur recall 100% hai
Accuracy 98% hai par recall 0 hai: ek bhi defaulter nahi pakda
Precision 98% aur recall 98% hai
questions.explanation: Saare predictions negative hain: 98% sahi (TN), isliye accuracy 98%; par TP = 0, toh recall = 0 / (0 + FN) = 0, option C. Imbalanced data me accuracy dhokha deti hai. Trap: option A sirf accuracy dekhta hai; option B positive aur negative class ulat deta hai; option D precision define hi nahi hota jab koi positive prediction hi na ho.

questions.question: Ek lender ke liye ek defaulter ko loan de dena (FN) ₹50,000 ka nuksaan hai, aur ek achhe applicant ko reject karna (FP) ₹5,000 ka khoya hua profit hai. Expected cost minimise karne ke liye default probability ke kis threshold se upar application reject karni chahiye?
questions.explanation: Reject karne ki expected cost = (1 − p) × 5,000; approve karne ki = p × 50,000. Reject tab jab p × 50,000 > (1 − p) × 5,000, yaani p > 5,000 / (5,000 + 50,000) ≈ 0.091, option A. Trap: option B default 0.5 hai jo dono costs ko barabar maanta hai; option C ratio ulta le leta hai (50,000 / 55,000); option D denominator me sirf C_FN leta hai (5,000 / 50,000).

questions.question: Ek analyst 'loan default hoga ya nahi' (1/0) ko linear regression se model karta hai. Is approach ki sabse badi problem kya hai?
options: Linear regression me numeric predictors use nahi ho sakte
Linear regression ka R² binary outcome pe hamesha 0 aata hai
Predictions 0 se kam ya 1 se zyada aa sakti hain
Linear regression sirf time series data pe chalta hai
questions.explanation: Binary outcome pe straight line kuch applicants ke liye p < 0 ya p > 1 de sakti hai, aur error variance p(1 − p) pe depend karta hai; logistic model hamesha 0–1 ke beech probability deta hai: option C. Trap: option B sun ke technical lagta hai par galat hai (R² positive aa sakta hai); options A aur D linear regression ke baare me galat facts hain.

questions.question: Ek logistic churn model me ek customer ke liye linear part z = β₀ + β₁x₁ + … ki value 0 aati hai. Uski churn probability kya hai?
options: Bina coefficients jaane nahi bata sakte
questions.explanation: p = 1 / (1 + e^(−z)); z = 0 pe e^0 = 1, toh p = 1 / 2 = 0.5 (option B). Trap: option A z ko hi probability maan leta hai; option D sochta hai ki coefficients chahiye, jabki z already de diya hai; option C bade positive z ka limit hai.

questions.question: Ek bank credit-card default model bana raha hai (outcome: agle 6 mahine me default). Inme se kaunsa predictor **data leakage** hai?
options: Application ke time customer ki monthly income
Pichhle 12 mahine me late payments ki sankhya
Application ke time credit utilisation ratio
Account collections team ko assign hua ya nahi
questions.explanation: Collections team ko account tab assign hota hai jab default ho chuka ya hone wala ho, yaani yeh outcome ke baad bani information hai: option D leakage hai aur test pe fake-good performance dega. Trap: option B bhi 'bad behaviour' lagta hai, par yeh application se pehle ka history hai, isliye valid predictor hai; options A aur C bhi decision ke time available hain.

questions.question: Ek churn model ke 500 customers ke test pe: TP = 45, FN = 15, FP = 30, TN = 410. Specificity aur accuracy kya hain?
options: Specificity ≈ 0.93, accuracy = 0.91
Specificity = 0.75, accuracy = 0.91
Specificity ≈ 0.93, accuracy = 0.82
Specificity = 0.60, accuracy ≈ 0.93
questions.explanation: Specificity = TN / (TN + FP) = 410 / 440 ≈ 0.93. Accuracy = (TP + TN) / N = (45 + 410) / 500 = 0.91: option A. Trap: option B me 0.75 recall hai (45 / 60), specificity nahi; option D me 0.60 precision hai (45 / 75); option C ka accuracy galat jodne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek churn model ka holdout AUC = 0.80 hai. Iska sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Model saare customers me se 80% ko sahi classify karta hai
0.5 threshold pe recall 80% hai, yaani 80% churners pakde
Churn karne wale 80% customers ki predicted probability 0.5 se upar hai
Churner ko non-churner se upar rank karne ka chance 0.80 hai
questions.explanation: AUC ek ranking measure hai: ek random positive (churner) aur ek random negative lo, toh 80% baar model churner ko zyada score dega: option D. Yeh kisi ek threshold pe depend nahi karta. Trap: option A AUC ko accuracy samajh leta hai; options B aur C ek specific threshold ki baat karte hain, jabki ROC curve saare thresholds ko summarise karti hai.

questions.question: Ek insurance lead ke policy khareedne ki baseline probability 0.2 hai. 'Callback request kiya' dummy ka odds ratio 3 hai. Callback request karne wale lead ki probability kya hai (baaki same)?
questions.explanation: Baseline odds = 0.2 / 0.8 = 0.25. Naye odds = 0.25 × 3 = 0.75. p = 0.75 / (1 + 0.75) ≈ 0.43: option B. Trap: option A odds ratio ko probability pe laga deta hai (0.2 × 3), jo classic galti hai; option C naye odds ko hi probability bol deta hai; option D sirf andaaza hai.

questions.question: Churn model: ln(p / (1 − p)) = −1.5 + 0.6·LatePayments − 0.02·Tenure (months). Ek customer ke 2 late payments aur 30 months tenure hai. Customer value ₹4,000, retention offer ₹250 ka, aur offer 25% churners ko rok leta hai. Kya offer dena chahiye?
options: p ≈ 0.29; expected benefit ≈ ₹289 > ₹250, offer do
p ≈ 0.71; expected benefit ≈ ₹711, offer do
p ≈ 0.29; expected benefit ≈ ₹1,156, offer do
p ≈ 0.41; expected benefit ≈ ₹407, offer do
questions.explanation: z = −1.5 + 0.6 × 2 − 0.02 × 30 = −1.5 + 1.2 − 0.6 = −0.9. p = 1 / (1 + e^0.9) ≈ 0.289. Expected benefit = 0.289 × 4,000 × 0.25 ≈ ₹289 > ₹250, toh offer profitable hai: option A. Trap: option B 1 − p le leta hai (sign ulta); option C save rate 25% bhool jaata hai; option D odds e^(−0.9) ≈ 0.41 ko probability maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek fraud model ne 100 transactions flag kiye, jinme se 60 asli fraud the. Test set me total 150 fraud transactions the. Model ka F1 score kya hai?
questions.explanation: TP = 60, FP = 40, FN = 150 − 60 = 90. Precision = 60 / 100 = 0.6, recall = 60 / 150 = 0.4. F1 = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 / (0.6 + 0.4) = 0.48: option C. Trap: option A arithmetic mean (0.6 + 0.4) / 2 hai, harmonic nahi; option B precision × recall hai, 2 aur denominator bhool gaya; option D sirf recall hai.

questions.question: Ek OTT app ke liye bekaar retention offer (FP) ki cost ₹200 hai, aur ek churner ko miss karna (FN) ₹1,800 ka nuksaan hai. Chaar customers ki churn probabilities: 0.08, 0.15, 0.40, 0.06. Expected cost minimise karne ke liye kitne customers ko offer milna chahiye?
options: Kisi ko nahi, kyunki sabki probability 0.5 se kam hai
Sirf 0.40 wale ko, kyunki threshold 0.25 hai
Chaaron ko, kyunki FN bahut mehnga hai
Do ko (0.15 aur 0.40), kyunki threshold 0.10 hai
questions.explanation: Threshold = C_FP / (C_FP + C_FN) = 200 / (200 + 1,800) = 0.10. Isse upar sirf 0.15 aur 0.40 hain, toh 2 customers: option D. Trap: option A default 0.5 threshold use karta hai jo yahan costs ko ignore karta hai; option C sochta hai ki mehnga FN matlab sabko offer, par 0.08 aur 0.06 wale pe expected loss offer cost se kam hai; option B ka threshold kisi formula se nahi aata.

weeks.title: Repeated ad exposure: within-subject designs and repeated-measures ANOVA
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki jab same customers ko kai conditions (jaise ad ko 1, 2, 3 baar dekhna) me measure karte hain toh within-subject design kyun zyada powerful hai, paired t-test aur repeated-measures ANOVA kaise karte hain, aur order effects, carryover aur sphericity jaise issues ko kaise handle karte hain.
concepts: **Between- vs within-subject design**: between-subject me har participant sirf ek condition dekhta hai (alag log, alag groups). **Within-subject (repeated measures)** me har participant saari conditions dekhta hai, jaise same 40 viewers ek ad ko 1, 2 aur 3 exposures ke baad rate karte hain. Har participant apna khud ka control ban jaata hai.

**Power kyun badhti hai**: log aapas me bahut alag hote hain (koi har ad ko 8/10 deta hai, koi 4/10). Between design me yeh person-to-person variation error me chala jaata hai. Within design me hum har person ka apna average level alag kar dete hain, isliye error chhota, F bada, aur kam participants me hi effect dikh jaata hai.

**Paired t-test** (2 conditions): har person ka difference dᵢ = after − before nikaalo, phir t = d̄ / (s_d / √n), df = n − 1. Yeh do 'independent' samples ka test nahi hai; same logon ke do measurements correlated hote hain, aur paired test isi correlation ka fayda uthata hai.

**Repeated-measures ANOVA** (k ≥ 2 conditions, n subjects): SST = SS_subjects + SS_conditions + SS_error. SS_conditions = n × Σ(condition mean − grand mean)², SS_subjects = k × Σ(subject mean − grand mean)², SS_error = baaki. **F = [SS_conditions / (k − 1)] / [SS_error / ((k − 1)(n − 1))]**. SS_subjects ko error se nikaal diya jaata hai, yahi fark hai.

**Sphericity**: RM-ANOVA assume karta hai ki har pair of conditions ke differences ka variance lagbhag barabar ho. Teen ya zyada conditions me yeh toote toh F-test zyada 'liberal' ho jaata hai; software Mauchly's test aur Greenhouse–Geisser correction (df ko ε < 1 se multiply karna) deta hai. 2 conditions me sphericity apne aap satisfy hoti hai.

**Order effects aur carryover**: same log baar-baar measure honge toh fatigue, learning ya pehli condition ka asar agli pe reh sakta hai. **Counterbalancing** (alag participants ko alag order, jaise Latin square), conditions ke beech gap (washout), aur jahan carryover unavoidable ho wahan between design behtar hai.

**Ad repetition ka business pattern (wear-in / wear-out)**: shuru me repetition se recall aur liking badhti hai (wear-in), par ek point ke baad irritation se liking girne lagti hai (wear-out), yaani aksar inverted-U shape. RM-ANOVA ke baad post-hoc / trend contrasts se dekhte hain ki peak kis exposure level pe hai, aur media plan me frequency cap wahi set karte hain.

example.problem: Megha Detergent (fictional) ka ad 4 participants ne 1, 2 aur 3 exposures ke baad liking scale (1–10) pe rate kiya. P1: 5, 7, 6; P2: 3, 5, 5; P3: 6, 8, 7; P4: 4, 6, 6. RM-ANOVA F nikaalo (F(2, 6) critical = 5.143), aur compare karo agar yahi data galti se 12 alag logon ka maan ke one-way ANOVA kiya jaata (F(2, 9) critical = 4.256).
steps: Grand mean = 68 / 12 ≈ 5.667. Condition means: 4.5, 6.5, 6.0. Subject means: 6, 4.33, 7, 5.33.
F = (8.67 / 2) / (0.67 / 6) = 4.33 / 0.111 ≈ 39.0 > 5.143 ⇒ exposure level ka effect significant.
Galat between-subject analysis: SSW = SS_subjects + SS_error = 12, df = 9, MSW = 1.333, F = 4.33 / 1.333 ≈ 3.25 < 4.256 ⇒ significant nahi dikhta.

**Answer**: RM-ANOVA **F ≈ 39.0** (significant); wahi data independent maan ke **F ≈ 3.25** (not significant). Person-to-person variation (SS_subjects = 11.33) hata dene se test kaafi zyada powerful ho gaya. Liking 2 exposures pe peak karke thodi girti hai: wear-out ka hint.

mistakes: Same participants ke before/after data pe two-sample (independent) t-test chalaana. Fix: paired t-test ya RM-ANOVA lo; independent test correlation ignore karta hai aur power kho deta hai.
Saare participants ko conditions ek hi order me dikhana. Fix: counterbalance karo, warna order effect aur condition effect mix ho jaate hain.
Teen ya zyada conditions me sphericity check kiye bina uncorrected F report karna. Fix: Mauchly's test dekho aur zaroorat ho toh Greenhouse–Geisser corrected p-value report karo.
revision: Within-subject: har person saari conditions; khud ka control.
Paired t = d̄ / (s_d / √n), df = n − 1.
SST = SS_subjects + SS_conditions + SS_error.
RM-ANOVA df = (k − 1, (k − 1)(n − 1)).
Sphericity toote ⇒ Greenhouse–Geisser correction.
Counterbalancing se order effects control; ad repetition aksar inverted-U.

questions.question: Ek FMCG company 40 customers ko teen packaging designs dikhati hai aur har customer teeno designs ko 1–10 pe rate karta hai. Yeh kis tarah ka design hai?
options: Between-subject design, 3 independent groups
Within-subject (repeated-measures) design
Cross-sectional observational survey jisme koi condition nahi
Matched-pairs design with 2 groups
questions.explanation: Har customer teeno conditions (designs) dekhta hai, toh har design ke ratings same logon se aate hain: within-subject (repeated-measures) design, option B. Trap: option A tab hota jab 40 customers ko teen alag groups me baant ke har group ko ek design dikhate; option D sirf 2 conditions aur alag-alag matched logon pe lagta hai.

questions.question: 10 participants ko ek ad 4 alag frequencies pe dikhaya gaya aur har frequency ke baad recall measure hua. Repeated-measures ANOVA ke F-statistic ke degrees of freedom kya hain?
questions.explanation: Conditions df = k − 1 = 3; error df = (k − 1)(n − 1) = 3 × 9 = 27, toh F(3, 27), option C. Trap: option A independent one-way ANOVA ka df (N − k = 40 − 4 = 36) leta hai, jo subjects ka variation error me hi rehne deta hai; option D sirf subjects ka df (n − 1) leta hai.

questions.question: 6 customers ka purchase intent (1–10) ad dekhne se pehle aur baad me measure hua. Har customer ke liye (after − before) differences: 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 4. Paired t-test (two-sided, α = 0.05, df = 5 pe critical 2.571) ka result kya hai?
options: t ≈ 3.46; ad ke baad intent significantly badha
t ≈ 1.41; significant nahi
t ≈ 8.49; significant
Paired test galat hai; before aur after ko do independent samples ki tarah test karna chahiye
questions.explanation: d̄ = 12 / 6 = 2; s_d = √(Σ(d − 2)² / 5) = √(10 / 5) ≈ 1.414; SE = 1.414 / √6 ≈ 0.577; t = 2 / 0.577 ≈ 3.46 > 2.571, option A. Trap: option B d̄ / s_d leta hai (√n bhool gaye); option C √n ki jagah n se divide karta hai; option D galat hai kyunki same customers ke do measurements correlated hain, isliye paired test hi sahi hai.

questions.question: 5 participants, 3 ad versions (sab participants ne teeno dekhe). RM-ANOVA me SS_conditions = 24, SS_subjects = 60, SS_error = 12. F-statistic kya hai?
questions.explanation: MS_conditions = 24 / (3 − 1) = 12; error df = (3 − 1)(5 − 1) = 8, MS_error = 12 / 8 = 1.5; F = 12 / 1.5 = 8.0, option D. Trap: option A subjects ka SS bhi error me daal deta hai (72 / 12 = 6, F = 12 / 6 = 2), jo independent ANOVA jaisa hai; option C SS_conditions ko df se divide karna bhool jaata hai (24 / 1.5); option B SS_conditions / SS_subjects leta hai.

questions.question: Ek ad-testing study me har participant pehle 15-second version aur phir 30-second version dekhta hai, aur 30-second version ko consistently zyada liking milti hai. Is result pe sabse bada sawaal kya hai, aur uska fix kya hai?
options: Sample size chhota hai; participants double karo
Sphericity toot gayi hai; Greenhouse–Geisser correction lagao
Liking scale ordinal hai; chi-square test lagao
Order / carryover effect: dusre ad tak brand familiar ho chuka tha; counterbalancing karo (aadhe log pehle 30-second dekhein)
questions.explanation: Saare participants ne same order dekha, toh 30-second version ka fayda asal me 'doosri baar brand dekhna' (familiarity / carryover) bhi ho sakta hai: condition aur order confounded hain. Counterbalancing (aadhe log ulta order) se yeh alag hota hai, option D. Trap: option B lagta hai, par 2 conditions me sphericity apne aap satisfy hoti hai; option A sample badhane se confounding nahi jaata.

questions.question: Ek ad agency kehti hai ki within-subject design me kam participants se bhi effect pakad me aa jaata hai. Iski sabse sahi wajah kya hai?

Within design me participants hamesha zyada honest jawab dete hain
Within design me order effects kabhi nahi hote
Within design me sphericity assumption ki zaroorat nahi hoti

Trap: option C ulta hai, within design me hi order aur carryover ka risk hota hai; option D bhi galat hai, 3+ conditions me sphericity zaroori hai; option B ka koi aadhaar nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kis repeated-measures study me sphericity check karne ki zaroorat **nahi** hai?
options: 30 viewers, 4 ad lengths ka liking score
20 shoppers, 3 store layouts ka basket value
25 customers, sirf 2 conditions: ad se pehle aur baad
40 users, 5 app themes ka satisfaction score
questions.explanation: Sphericity ka matlab hai ki har pair of conditions ke differences ka variance barabar ho. Sirf 2 conditions me ek hi difference hota hai, isliye yeh apne aap satisfy hoti hai: option C. Trap: options A, B aur D me 3 ya zyada conditions hain, wahan Mauchly's test aur zaroorat ho toh Greenhouse–Geisser correction chahiye; participants ki sankhya isse tay nahi karti.

questions.question: Ek RM-ANOVA study me ek ad ke liking ke means 1 se 5 exposures pe: 5.2, 6.4, 6.9, 6.5, 5.8. Media plan me frequency cap kitne exposures pe rakhna sabse sensible hai?
options: 1 exposure, kyunki pehli baar ad naya hota hai
5 exposures, kyunki zyada exposure se zyada recall
3 exposures, jahan liking peak karti hai
2 exposures, kyunki 1 se 2 pe sabse bada jump hai
questions.explanation: Pattern inverted-U hai: 3 exposures tak liking badhti hai (wear-in) aur uske baad girti hai (wear-out), isliye cap peak pe, yaani 3 pe: option C. Trap: option D sabse bada increase dekhta hai, par 3 pe bhi liking badh rahi hai (6.4 → 6.9); option B wear-out ignore karta hai; option A wear-in ignore karta hai.

questions.question: 12 participants, 4 ad versions wale RM-ANOVA me Mauchly's test sphericity reject karta hai aur Greenhouse–Geisser ε = 0.6 hai. Corrected degrees of freedom kya honge?

Trap: option B correction lagata hi nahi; option C k = 4 ko ε se multiply karta hai (4 × 0.6) aur 44 × 0.6; option D sirf numerator correct karta hai.

t = 2.4; significant

questions.question: 5 customers ka brand-trust score ek CSR ad se pehle: 6, 4, 7, 5, 8 aur baad me (same order): 7, 6, 8, 5, 9. df = 4 pe two-sided 5% critical 2.776 hai. Paired t-test ka result kya hai, aur galti se independent t-test lagaate toh kya hota?

questions.question: 11 participants, 3 ad versions wale RM-ANOVA me SST = 100, SS_conditions = 20, SS_subjects = 50. RM-ANOVA ka F kya hai, aur agar same data ko galti se one-way between-subject ANOVA maan lein toh F kya aata?

Between ANOVA me SSW = SS_subjects + SS_error = 80, df = 33 − 3 = 30, MSW ≈ 2.67, F = 10 / 2.67 = 3.75: option A. questions.question: 24 participants 4 ad versions (A, B, C, D) dekhenge. Order effects ke liye Latin square counterbalancing use karni hai. Kitne alag orders chahiye, har order me kitne participants, aur design kya guarantee karta hai?
options: 24 orders, har order me 1 participant; har possible sequence ek baar
